{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:26:47.177619+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f6cf902830d44196232726e732f11132c890f43f7349e2277ad075f47de1989b","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem 78 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For $\hat{Y}$ the stopped martingale defined above, we can construct a deterministic time change $\tilde{Y}$ that can be expressed as the stochastic integral
    \[
    \tilde{Y}(t)
    =\tilde{Y}(q_0) + \int_0^t \tilde{w}_t\,d\tilde{W}(t)
    \]
for $t\in[q_0,\gamma(1)]$,
where
$\tilde{Y}(q_0)=\hat{Y}(q_0)=Y(q_0)$,
$\tilde{W}$ is a standard Brownian motion, and $\tilde{w}$ satisfies
the constraint $\E[(\tilde{w}_t)^2]=1$ for all $t\in[q_0,\gamma(1)]$.

\begin{proof} We will construct a  martingale $\tilde{Y}$ to essentially be the deterministic time-change of $\hat{Y}$ such that $\E[\tilde{Y}(t)^2]=t$ for all $t\in[q_0,\gamma(1)]$. Then, for $t\in[\gamma(1),1]$, we will take $\tilde{Y}$ to be any martingale ending at $\pm1$ almost surely, which exists by Lemma~\ref{lem:Yt-process-always-is-completable} below. To formalize the time reparametrization, since $\gamma:[q_0,1]\to[q_0,\gamma(1)]$ is nondecreasing, we can define its right-continuous generalized inverse 
\[\lambda:[q_0,\gamma(1)]\to[q_0,1]\,.\]
As a consequence of \eqref{e:gamma.prime} we must have $\gamma(t)-\gamma(s)\le t-s$ and $\lambda(t)-\lambda(s)\ge t-s$ for all $q_0 \le s\le t\le1$. It  follows by combining these inequalities with Proposition~\ref{p:gamma-1} that
    \beq
    \begin{aligned}
    s &\ge \gamma(s) \ge \gamma(1)+s-1 \ge s-4\epsilon^{1/2}\,,\\
    t &\le \lambda(t) \le \lambda(\gamma(1)) + t-\gamma(1)
    =1+t-\gamma(1) \le t+4\epsilon^{1/2}
    \end{aligned}
    \eeq
for all $s\in [q_0,1]$, and $t\in [q_0,\gamma(1)]$. It is clear from this that we must define $\tilde{Y}(t) = \hat{Y}(\lambda(t))$, so that
we will have $\E[\tilde{Y}(t)^2] = \E[\hat{Y}(\lambda(t))^2] = \gamma(\lambda(t))=t$. Since
    \[
    \hat{Y}(\lambda(t)) = Y(q_0) + \int_{q_0}^{\lambda(t)}
        w_u \ind\{u\le\tau\} \,dW(u)\,,
    \]
by considering the change of variables $u=\lambda(s)$ it is natural to define
    \beq
    \tilde{W}(t) = \int_{q_0}^{\lambda(t)} \gamma'(u)^{1/2} dW(u)\,.
    \eeq
Then $\tilde{W}$ is a local martingale with quadratic variation
    \[
    \langle \tilde{W}\rangle_t 
    = \int_{q_0}^{\lambda(t)} \gamma'(u)\,du
    = \gamma(\lambda(t))-\gamma(q_0) = t-q_0
    \]
for all $t\in[q_0,1]$, so by the L\'evy characterization it is a standard Brownian motion on $t\in[q_0,1]$, and is progressively measurable with respect to the time-changed filtration
$\tilde{\cF}_Y(t)\equiv\cF_Y(\lambda(t))$. We then define the modified control
    \[
    \tilde{w}_s
    \equiv
    \frac{w_{\lambda(s)}}{\gamma'(\lambda(s))^{1/2} }
      \ind\{\lambda(s)\le \tau\}\,,\]
where we define $\tilde{w}_s\equiv1$ in the case $\gamma'(\lambda(s))=0$ --- by Lemma~\ref{l:generalized.inverse.fn}, the set of such times $s$ is of measure zero. If $\gamma'(\lambda(s))=0$ then clearly we have $\E[(\tilde{w}_s)^2]=1$, and otherwise 
\eqref{e:gamma.prime} gives
	\[\E[(\tilde{w}_s)^2]
    =\frac{\E[(w_{\lambda(s)})^2 \ind\{
        \lambda(s)\le\tau\}]}
        {\gamma'(\lambda(s))}
    = 1\,.
    \]
We can then express the desired process as
    \[
    \tilde{Y}(t)
    = \hat{Y}(\lambda(t))
    =\tilde{Y}(q_0) + \int_{q_0}^t \tilde{w}_s\,d\tilde{W}(s)\,,
    \]
where $\tilde{Y}(q_0)=\hat{Y}(q_0)= Y(q_0)$. This concludes the proof.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

Banks, J. Garza-Vargas, A. Kulkarni, N. Srivastava, Overlaps, eigenvalue gaps, and pseudospectrum under real Ginibre and absolutely continuous perturbations, arXiv:2005.08930, Corollary 2.4; Theorem 2.1 there treats matrices X, Y in R^{n x k}). {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:16:18.664083+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f70c928b376b6f60597a43fae1e743d3682e0d69eac9b55e32d06b808cd26188","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 8 of arXiv:2607.25645, 'Estimates of the total variation distance between laws of Sobolev mappings on Gaussian spa'] Let $k,d\in\mathbb{N}$ with $d\ge 2$, and let $a,b>0$. Set
\[
\beta_1:=\frac{1}{2k(d-1)+1}
\quad\text{and}\quad
s:=\frac{d(2k-1)}{4k(d-1)}.
\]
Then, for every pair of mappings $f=(f_1,\ldots,f_k)$ and $g=(g_1,\ldots,g_k)$ with
$f_j,g_j\in \mathcal{P}_d(\gamma)$,
\[
\int_E \Delta_f\,d\gamma\ge a,
\quad
\int_E \Delta_g\,d\gamma\ge a,
\]
and
\[
\max_{1\le j\le k}\operatorname{Var}_\gamma(f_j)\le b,
\quad
\max_{1\le j\le k}\operatorname{Var}_\gamma(g_j)\le b,
\]
one has, for every $\beta\in(0,\beta_1)$,
\begin{equation}
d_{\mathrm{TV}}(f,g)
\le
C_1k^{3/2}d\,(\beta_1-\beta)^{-s}
\bigl(1+a^{-\frac{1}{2k(d-1)}}b^{\frac{2k-1}{4k(d-1)}}\bigr)\,
d_{\mathrm{KR}}(f,g)^\beta,
\end{equation}
where $C_1>0$ is an absolute constant. In particular, if $d_{\mathrm{KR}}(f,g)>0$, then
\begin{equation}
d_{\mathrm{TV}}(f,g)
\le
C_2k^{3/2}d
\bigl(1+a^{-\frac{1}{2k(d-1)}}b^{\frac{2k-1}{4k(d-1)}}\bigr)
\bigl(1+\ln\tfrac{2}{d_{\mathrm{KR}}(f,g)}\bigr)^s
d_{\mathrm{KR}}(f,g)^{\beta_1},
\end{equation}
where $C_2>0$ is an absolute constant.

More generally, for every $r\in\mathbb{N}$, setting
\[
\beta_r:=\frac{1}{2rk(d-1)+1},
\]
one has, for every $\beta\in(0,\beta_r)$,
\begin{equation}
d_{\mathrm{TV}}(f,g)
\le
C_1(r,k)\,d\,(\beta_r-\beta)^{-s}
\bigl(1+a^{-\frac{1}{2k(d-1)}}b^{\frac{2k-1}{4k(d-1)}}\bigr)\,
d_r(f,g)^\beta,
\end{equation}
where $C_1(r,k)>0$ depends only on $r$ and $k$. Moreover, if $d_r(f,g)>0$, then
\begin{equation}
d_{\mathrm{TV}}(f,g)
\le
C_2(r,k)\,d
\bigl(1+a^{-\frac{1}{2k(d-1)}}b^{\frac{2k-1}{4k(d-1)}}\bigr)
\bigl(1+\ln\tfrac{2}{d_r(f,g)}\bigr)^s
d_r(f,g)^{\beta_r},
\end{equation}
where $C_2(r,k)>0$ depends only on $r$ and $k$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:38:13.648450+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f721a0fc3932ce77e99e32722ed09256cb9bcf14c3dc9fea1afe7a28652e1337","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defn 9 of arXiv:2609.00723, 'An integral Hyodo--Kato isomorphism'] [See \cite[Definitions~3.8, 3.9 and 3.11]{Ya}.]

\[
\sA^*=(A^*,d,F,\alpha:L\to A^0,\delta:L\to A^1)
\]
over $\sR$ is \emph{saturated} if its underlying Dieudonn\'e algebra is

\[

\]

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T15:32:35.579901+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f72476ea5c1f80b99b0a20816b02be7cd0cadac4de38b1a46bfc46c40a0d11d9","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Prop u11 of arXiv:2606.06187, 'How to Study Reflected Brownian Motion in a Quadrant via Kernel Functional Equations?\\ \m'] Assume that the existence condition~(equation intro:existence of the paper) is satisfied and that the drift $\mu$ is non-zero.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:51:11.643858+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f74cebb82afe43a42a2c76e3f62e0debe1495ee8bf0289ca82d55627e735df2c","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 21 of arXiv:2605.31471, 'Convergence Rates of Continuous-Time Random Walks to Time-Fractional Diffusions with Unbou'] Let $F_t = e^{tL}$ be a strongly continuous bounded semigroup on a Banach space $(B,\|\cdot\|_B)$:
        \[
            \max_{s \in [0,t]} \|F_s\|_{B \to B} \leq e^{\bar m t}.
        \]
        
        Let $L$ be the generator of $F_t$, and let $D \subset \operatorname{dom} L$ be another Banach space with $\|\cdot\|_D \geq \|\cdot\|_B$ such that
        \[
        \|Lf\|_B \leq l \|f\|_D \, \forall f \in D.
        \]
        Assume also that $F_t$ is bounded in $D$:
        \[
        \max_{s \in [0,t]} \|F_s\|_{D \to D} \leq e^{m t},
        \]
        for some $m \geq 0$.
        
        
        Let $U_h$ be a family of linear bounded operators in $B$ with 
        \[
          \| U_h \|_{B \to B} \leq e^{q h},
          \qquad q\ge0,
        \]
        and let
        \begin{align} 
        \left\| \left( \frac{U_h - 1}{h} - L \right) f \right\|_B &\leq \epsilon_h \|f\|_D, \\
        
        \left\| \left( \frac{F_h - 1}{h} - L \right) f \right\|_B &\leq \chi_h \|f\|_D, 
        \end{align}
        where $\epsilon_h,\chi_h>0$ are monotone and tend to zero as $h\to0$.
        
        Then
        \begin{equation} 
        \begin{aligned}
            \sup_{s \leq t} \left\| (U_h)^{\lfloor s/h\rfloor} f - F_s f \right\|_B
            &\leq
            (\chi_h + \epsilon_h) \|f\|_D
            \int_0^t e^{ms + q (t-s)} \, ds  \\
            &\quad
            + e^{\bar m t} h (l + \epsilon_h) \|f\|_D .
        \end{aligned}
        \end{equation}

        For the killed semigroups with rate $c>0$,
        \begin{equation} 
        \begin{aligned}
            \sup_{s \leq t}
            \left\| e^{-c\lfloor s/h\rfloor h } (U_h)^{\lfloor s/h\rfloor} f
            - e^{-cs} F_s f \right\|_B
            &\leq
            (\chi_h + \epsilon_h) \|f\|_D
            \int_0^t e^{(m-c)s + (q-c) (t-s)} \, ds  \\
            &\quad
            + e^{(\bar m - c) t} h (l + \epsilon_h + c) \|f\|_D .
        \end{aligned}
        \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["d>=1,N>=2d+1,n>=0,K>=2,1<=r<K,0<=ell<=r integers","Paired A/S VC class; uniform contexts then uniform truths; independent uniform r-subsets in A, all truths in S","Actual iid factual samples without tags; independent uniform ell-subset verifier in every variable context including S","Unresolved sibling pairs have equal distinct observed-plus-certified counts h<=r; identified pairs are logically certified by an S context with >r known truths; each identified A count j is >= maximum unresolved h (vacuous if none)","All generators; robust exact-level source calibration across every compatible orientation and residual support"],"created_at":"2026-10-21T21:03:39.295480+00:00","domain":"statistical learning; calibrated generation; partial truth verification","id":"claim_f75b182c10094807f8f65295a7c116ffcea2d51b7b906b0cc0c6c75d7a006c10","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"Own-work draft; proof (unaudited); independent review pending. # Pair-balanced factual identities under partial verification

T379-C015 v2, proof (unaudited). Both exact verification suites PASS;
independent mathematical, priority and target-scope review pending.
Targets 1 and 2. This is a conditional data-regime result, not a global
expected minimax claim. The unresolved unequal-sibling-count regime is
the hardest missing piece; C010 shows why its ordering cannot be assumed.

## Model and data region

Use the paired VC-d experiment: d>=1,N>=2d+1,K>=2,1<=r<K integers;
one A and one S per pair, all remaining contexts known S. S has K true
candidates, A has an independent uniform r-subset. The source p chooses
contexts uniformly, then true candidates uniformly. Observe n>=0 iid
factual context/candidate samples without orientation tags. Independently
a perfect verifier supplies a uniform ell-subset of truths in each
variable context, including S, 0<=ell<=r. Let C_x be the union of
distinct observed and verified candidate identities in context x.

Condition on any positive-probability data outcome for which every pair
has |C_left|=|C_right|=h_j<=r. The actual identities may differ. Thus no
orientation is logically excluded, and every one of 2^d orientations
is compatible. Counts and likelihoods of repeated observations can be
unequal: uniform orientation weights below are an ARTIFICIAL proof
distribution, not the actual Bayesian posterior. Under a chosen
orientation, the A support ranges uniformly over r-subsets containing
C_A. Put D_h=#{j:h_j=h}, ell<=h<=r.

Define

 b_h=[1/K+(r-h)/(r(K-h))]/(2N),
 tau_h=(K-r)/(2(K-h)),
 M_h=(D_h/N)*(2-h/r-h/K),
 T_h=sum_{t=h}^r M_t.

Over ALL generators, with source Mis_infinity<=c required in every
compatible world (including every compatible A support), the proposed
exact conditional worst-world false-mass frontier is

 V_D(c)=tau_ell*(T_ell-c)_+
        +sum_{h=ell+1}^r (tau_h-tau_{h-1})*(T_h-c)_+.       (1)

All formulas allow missing D_h and c in [0,1]. Exact score bins define
source Mis_infinity=TV(g,p_Pi), with p uniformly coarsened in each bin.

## Lower bound across arbitrary mixed bins

Average orientations fairly and A supports uniformly conditional on
containing their known identities. Let mu be the resulting mean law.
Every known true atom in a variable context has density

 a=(1/r+1/K)/(2N).

The uncertified atoms of a pair at count h have density b_h and false
probability tau_h under this artificial prior. Their total mu mass is
M_h across the D_h pairs. Known S atoms have density 1/(NK).

As h increases, tau_h increases and b_h decreases: directly,
b_h-b_{h+1}=(K-r)/(2Nr(K-h)(K-h-1)) when h<r. All safe densities
are >=1/(NK)>=b_h. Thus E_h, the union of uncertified atoms in pairs
with count at least h, consists of lower-density atoms than its entire
complement. For ANY partition Pi, uniform coarsening increases its mass:

 mu_Pi(E_h)>=mu(E_h)=T_h.

Indeed in each cell the mean density over E_h is at most the mean over
its complement, so replacing both means by the cell mean transfers
mass into E_h. This proves the assertion per bin, not merely globally.

Robust feasibility and linearity/TV convexity give TV(mu_Pi(g),g)<=c.
Hence g(E_h)>=(T_h-c)_+. Layer-cake decomposition of the artificial
average false risk gives

 max_world H(g)>=tau_ell*g(E_ell)
                   +sum_{h>ell}(tau_h-tau_{h-1})*g(E_h)
                >=V_D(c).

No joint-probability multiplication or actual-posterior identity is used.

## Matching construction

Start from mu. Remove mass min(c,T_ell) from uncertified groups in
decreasing h order, uniformly within each h group, and add it uniformly
to the fixed known S reservoir. All remaining g(E_h)=(T_h-c)_+.
Each pair's known-true group has h atoms from each sibling and invariant
source mass h*(1/r+1/K)/N. Its uncertified group has K-h atoms from
each sibling and invariant source mass (2-h/r-h/K)/N, regardless of
orientation or which residual truths occupy A. The constructed g is
constant on every such group. Exact score bins only merge invariant
groups, so p_Pi=mu_Pi in every compatible world. Since g_Pi=g,
Mis_infinity<=TV(mu,g)<=c. The uncertified false-atom fraction in each
h group equals tau_h in every world. Thus actual H equals V_D(c)
worldwise, proving conditional sharpness of (1).

## Same-data oracle and exact estimation penalty

If the true partition is additionally supplied, let

 A_h=D_h*(r-h)/(Nr), Q_h=sum_{t=h}^r A_t,
 alpha_h=(K-r)/(K-h)=2tau_h.

The same-data known-partition frontier, by the ordered known-A groups,
is

 O_D(c)=alpha_ell*(Q_ell-c)_+
        +sum_{h>ell}(alpha_h-alpha_{h-1})*(Q_h-c)_+.       (2)

Here A_h is the posterior mass of unknown true candidates of the actual
A contexts, and their densities decrease while their false risks rise.
The same mixed-bin tail proof and transfer-to-S construction apply.
Thus V_D(c)=O_D(c)+[V_D(c)-O_D(c)] is an exact matching decomposition,
with nonnegative difference because giving the partition enlarges
feasibility. At c=0 it simplifies to the explicit positive penalty

 V_D(0)-O_D(0)
   =sum_{h=ell}^r D_h*h*(K-r)^2/(2NrK(K-h)).             (3)

The penalty is zero at h=0, and at h=r contributes kappa/(2N) per pair,
recovering C013's unresolved full-verifier value. In general it depends
on the factual-support histogram, not merely VC dimension or a single
unweighted classification-error scalar. A fair completion among the
2^d support-consistent ERM orientations has conditional expected
classification error 1/N per pair; (3) weights that error by
h*(K-r)^2/[2rK(K-h)]. This is a specified ERM, not an optimal posterior
classification claim. The conditional minimax lower bound is not
silently averaged into a global expected lower bound; C014 forbids
that shortcut at positive budgets.

## Scope

This removes supplied tags and retains actual factual identities for
every balanced outcome, all n,K,r,ell and all calibration budgets. It
allows different h across pairs, but does not cover unequal sibling
counts, already identified pairs, or an unconditional exact expected
frontier. Equal h in every pair reduces the conditional formula to the
corresponding earlier C008 experiment with that many known truths;
the histogram, actual untagged-data applicability and explicit oracle
penalty are the proposed extension, not a claim that C008 was unknown.
Primary basis: Kalai--Vempala 2311.14648v3 Definitions 1--2 pp.8--9;
own earlier C008/C009 are unaudited drafts. No novelty or target score
is certified until independent mathematical and priority review.

## Extension: include identified pairs under a coverage ordering

The same theorem extends as follows. Partition the d pairs into resolved
and unresolved pairs. A resolved pair has a context with >r distinct
known truths, logically forcing S and identifying its sibling as A.
Let E_j count these known A contexts with j distinct known truths,
ell<=j<=r. Each unresolved pair still has balanced count h<=r; D_h
now counts just these unresolved pairs. Require

 j>=h_max for every resolved A, where
 h_max=max{h:D_h>0}.                                    (4)

If no unresolved pairs exist, condition (4) is vacuous. Known facts
in identified S and fixed S contexts are all safe and have density
1/(NK), irrespective of their observed identities or counts.

There are two positive-risk group types under the artificial compatible
prior (independent fair unresolved orientations and uniform compatible
A supports):

* Unresolved count h: mass M_h as before, risk tau_h, density b_h.
* Resolved A count j: mass L_j=E_j*(r-j)/(Nr), risk
  alpha_j=(K-r)/(K-j), density a_j=(r-j)/(Nr(K-j)).

Groups at j=r can have zero factual mass and risk one; retain them
without dividing by their mass. All safe groups have density >=1/(NK).
For resolved groups, j increasing makes risk increase and density
decrease. Across the two types condition (4) implies

 alpha_j>=alpha_hmax=2tau_hmax>=tau_h,
 a_j<=a_hmax<=b_hmax<=b_h.

Thus ALL groups are ordered in opposite directions by density and risk.
Let 0<xi_1<...<xi_s<=1 be their distinct risk values; aggregate masses
at equal risk into m_i, and let R_i=sum_{k=i}^s m_k, xi_0=0. The exact
combined conditional robust frontier is

 V(c)=sum_{i=1}^s (xi_i-xi_{i-1})*(R_i-c)_+.             (5)

The same arbitrary-bin tail argument proves the lower bound. Remove
mass in decreasing risk order, uniformly inside each group, and transfer
to fixed S for the upper bound. Resolved A certified and uncertified
groups have world-invariant p masses because all residual supports
have the same size and contain the known truths. Unresolved balanced
groups have the invariance proved earlier. Consequently exact score
mergers remain valid for every compatible support and orientation.
False fractions equal the specified risks in EACH actual world, so
the construction attains (5) worldwise, not just on artificial average.

The same-data partition oracle is formula (2) with A_h replaced by

 (D_h+E_h)*(r-h)/(Nr).

At c=0 its exact difference from (5) is still formula (3), now summed
over unresolved pairs only. The identified-pair terms cancel. At any
c, both explicit formulas match their respective conditional minima.
When ell=r, every resolved A has j=r and condition (4) always holds;
this reduces (5) to C013's conditional frontier for arbitrary mixtures
of resolved and unresolved pairs. For ell<r this is a larger untagged
partial-verifier data regime than the all-unresolved case.

Unequal sibling counts or failure of (4) are NOT covered. No exact
global expected minimax value follows by averaging (5). This extension
has a separate route check, logs/route_014_extension_check.txt, and its
finite exact verification is kept separate from the general derivation.

## Zero-budget pointwise scope and an explicit control

If all pairs are unresolved and share ONE count h, every atom of the
artificial mean law has density at least b_h. Robust zero calibration
implies g=mu_Pi, hence g(atom)>=b_h. Each actual world has exactly
d(K-r) false atoms. Consequently every such generator obeys the
POINTWISE bound H>=d(K-r)b_h=V_D(0), and the construction attains it.
This separate observation applies regardless of actual orientation
likelihoods. It does not extend to varying h by the same argument.

In fact varying h can destroy even a zero-budget pointwise version of
the conditional bound. Take N=5,d=2,K=3,r=2,ell=0 and counts h_0=0,
h_1=1; use C_2=C_3={0}. These are possible actual untagged data, e.g.
the two observations (2,0),(3,0). Form a bin B containing all three
atoms of context 0 and the four uncertified atoms of contexts 2 and 3.
Its source mass is 1/5+7/30=13/30, independent of orientations and
residual A supports; set g=13/210 on its seven atoms. Other bins are
all of context 1 (g=1/15), both certified atoms of contexts 2 and 3
(g=1/12), and all fixed-S context 4 (g=1/15). Merging the equal 1/15
scores preserves invariance. This g is robustly source-calibrated at
zero in every compatible world.

If context 0 is A its actual false mass is 13/105, strictly below
V_D(0)=1/8 by 1/840. If context 1 is A, its false mass is 9/70,
strictly above 1/8. This is a real compatible-world control, not a
violation of (1) or (5): the theorem is conditional WORST-WORLD, and
the latter world meets that lower bound. It forbids silently replacing
the conditional maximum by a per-world bound even at zero budget in
the varying-count family. No claim about the global sampling minimax
value follows from this single outcome.

show actual failure of score-bin invariance without pair balance,
density ordering without sufficient identified-A coverage, and the
zero-budget pointwise extension under varying pair counts. Finite
verification supports, and does not replace, the general proof above.","status":"unverified"}

Meanwhile, if $\ell \ge (1+\varepsilon)\frac{\log 2}{2} \frac{n}{\log n}$, then $\chi_{\text{avg}}^2(\ell) \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$. Therefore, there is some sequence of starting states $x^{(n)} \in C_2^n$ such that $\chi_{x^{(n)}}^2(\ell) \to \infty$ even after $(1 - \varepsilon)\frac{\log 2}{2} \frac{n}{\log n}$ steps, while all starting states $x$ have $\chi_x^2(\ell) \to 0$ after just $(1 + \varepsilon)\frac{\log 2}{2} \frac{n}{\log n}$ steps. 
    \item Let $x^{(n)} \in C_2^n$ be any sequence of states such that $cn \le |x^{(n)}| \le (1 - c)n$ for some $c \in (0, 1)$ (where $|x|$ denotes the number of ones in $x$). Then $\chi_{x^{(n)}}^2(\ell) \to \infty$ for $\ell = \Theta_c\left(\frac{n}{\log n}\right)$ (that is, after order $\frac{n}{\log n}$ steps with constant depending only on $c$). 
    \item In particular, let $y^{(n)} \in C_2^n$ be the states with $\lfloor \frac{n}{2} \rfloor$ zeros followed by $\lceil \frac{n}{2} \rceil$ ones. Then $\chi_{y^{(n)}}^2(\ell) \to \infty$ for $\ell \le (1-\varepsilon) \frac{\log 2}{2} \frac{n}{\log n}$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["continuous-time nearest-neighbour walk on Z at rate 1 each side","killing rate kappa everywhere plus extra rate v at the origin","lambda = kappa"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T19:11:19.449396+00:00","domain":"probability, Markov chains, quasi-stationarity","id":"claim_f79d71e760cf075bc4e18baaa05fffea3c0cb7fb5e81cb05a97d33d3c8eca69c","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Pollett's Section 2 conjecture (ii) asks whether, for a lambda-transient irreducible countable transient class with almost sure absorption, every finite strictly positive limit of t^a e^{lambda t} p_t(i,j) must factor as A x_i m_j. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:49:49.204465+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f7eb8993ced6a5a30eaf669e1d59bbb453f63aab5960c3325dfbe770e82ab095","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 6 (Matrix Freedman) of arXiv:2604.27119, '\Large Applied Random Matrix Theory\relatedversion'] Consider a finite matrix martingale sequence $(\mtx{S}_0, \dots, \mtx{S}_n)$
consisting of $d_1 \times d_2$ matrices, real or complex.

Suppose that the elements of the difference sequence 
$(\mtx{X}_1, \dots, \mtx{X}_n)$ are uniformly bounded:
$\norm{ \mtx{X}_k } \leq B$.

Introduce the \term{conditional quadratic variation} sequence:
\[
V_k \coloneqq
	\lnorm{ \sum_{j=1}^k \Expect\big[ \mtx{X}_j \mtx{X}_j^* \condbar \coll{F}_{j-1} \big] }
	\vee \lnorm{ \sum_{j=1}^k \Expect\big[ \mtx{X}_j^* \mtx{X}_j \condbar \coll{F}_{j-1} \big] }
	\quad\text{for $k = 1, \dots, n$.}
\]
For parameters $v, t \geq 0$, we have the probability inequalities
\begin{align}

\Prob{ \exists k : \norm{\mtx{S}_k - \mtx{S}_0 } \geq \sqrt{2 v t} + Bt/3 \ \text{and} \
	V_k \leq v } &\leq (d_1+d_2) \, \econst^{-t}; \\

\Prob{ \exists k : \norm{\mtx{S}_k - \mtx{S}_0 } \geq t \ \text{and} \
	V_k \leq v } &\leq (d_1+d_2) \exp\left( \frac{-t^2/2}{v + Bt/3} \right).
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T23:48:35.820831+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f8133eb2abaaa0d099df45667c7e5cd34a5973f80e5f7bb261d591ebb82917af","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma Analogue of lemma 3.9 of arXiv:2411.09614, 'Moment estimates for the stochastic heat equation on Cartan-Hadamard manifolds'] Suppose $u_0\in L^\infty(M)\cap L^r(M)$, $1\leq r\leq +\infty$.
    Let $b=b(r)=\frac{(n-1)^2}{2\max(2,r)}K_1$ (it is 0 if $r=+\infty$). There exist three functions $F_1,F_2,F_3:\mathbb{R}_+\to\mathbb{R}_+$ such that for every $t>0$, $x\in M$, the following holds for $\alpha>\frac{n-2}{4}$ and $\rho >0$,
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
        \item If $\frac{n-2}{4}<\alpha<\frac{n}{4}$, $$\norm{f_k(\cdot,t,x)}_{\mathcal{H}^{\otimes k}}^2\leq C^k e^{-2bt}\frac{\beta^{2k}}{k!}\norm{u_0}_{\infty}^2e^{\rho t}F_1(\rho)^k.$$
        \item If $\alpha=\frac{n}{4}$, $$\norm{f_k(\cdot,t,x)}_{\mathcal{H}^{\otimes k}}^2\leq C^k e^{-2bt}\frac{\beta^{2k}}{k!}\norm{u_0}_{\infty}^2e^{\rho t}F_2(\rho)^k.$$

        Note that this implies $F_i:\mathbb{R}_+\to (0,F_i(0)]$ is invertible.

                \frac{(\ln \rho)^2}{\rho}& i=2,\\

            \end{cases}
    \end{equation}
    \end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:33:43.754244+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f83851b512d3b194792166811452355affca69897551a1a76d2fd6a77e95612c","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition prop:existence_measure_initial of arXiv:2609.01984, 'Instantaneous shrinking of supports for stochastic PDEs\footnote{JY was supported by a KIA'] There exist a filtered probability space, a space-time white noise $\widetilde\xi$, a nonnegative random Radon measure $\widetilde\mu_0$, a coefficient field $(\widetilde a,\widetilde b,\widetilde c) $ satisfying Assumption~(asp:coefficients of the paper), and a nonnegative process

\ u\in C((0,T];C_{\mathrm{tem}})

\[

\]

        \sup_{0<t\le T} W_q(u(t))^\alpha

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T23:00:22.773837+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f840aba8091a8a2b7dce79ad04d35a350c748311bd87024ae5a290682e00ec1d","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:multi-well of arXiv:2411.01364, 'Global Dynamics of Granular Media Equations via Stochastic Order'] Consider the following one-dimensional McKean-Vlasov SDE,
\begin{equation}
\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} X_t=-\left[X_t(X_t-1)(X_t+1)(X_t-2)(X_t+2)+\theta\left(X_t-\mathbf E [X_t]\right)\right]\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} t+\sigma(X_t)\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} B_t.
\end{equation}
If the parameter $\theta$ and the Lipschitz function $\sigma\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ satisfy
\[
\theta\geq8\sqrt{5+\sqrt{13}},\quad 0<\inf_{x\in\mathbb R}\sigma^2(x)\leq \sup_{x\in\mathbb R}\sigma^2(x)<\frac{4(13\sqrt{13}-35)}{27},
\]
and let $r=\frac{\sqrt{15-3\sqrt{13}}}{3}$, then 
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(\roman*)}]
\item There are exactly five invariant measures, $\nu_{-2}, \nu_{-1}, \nu_0, \nu_1, \nu_2\in\mathcal P_{\8}(\mathbb R)$ with $\nu_{-2}<_{\mathrm{st}}\nu_{-1}<_{\mathrm{st}}\nu_0<_{\mathrm{st}}\nu_1<_{\mathrm{st}}\nu_2$;
\item For all bounded sets $B\subset\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R)$, $\mathcal W_2(P_t^*B,[\nu_{-2},\nu_2])\to0$ as $t\to\8$;
\item There are a decreasing connecting orbit from $\nu_{-1}$ to $\nu_{-2}$ and an increasing connecting orbit from $\nu_{-1}$ to $\nu_0$;\\
there are a decreasing connecting orbit from $\nu_1$ to $\nu_0$ and an increasing connecting orbit from $\nu_1$ to $\nu_2$;
\item There hold $\nu_{-2}\in B(\delta_{-2},r)$, $\nu_0\in B(\delta_0,r)$, $\nu_2\in B(\delta_2,r)$, and
\[
\mathcal W_2(P_t^*\mu,\nu_{-2})\to0\ \text{ as $t\to\8$ for all $\mu\in\bigcup_{a\leq0}B(\delta_{-2+a},r)$},
\]
\[
\mathcal W_2(P_t^*\mu,\nu_{0})\to0\ \text{ as $t\to\8$ for all $\mu\in B(\delta_{0},r)$},
\]
and
\[
\mathcal W_2(P_t^*\mu,\nu_2)\to0\ \text{ as $t\to\8$ for all $\mu\in\bigcup_{a\geq0}B(\delta_{2+a},r)$}.
\]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:37:08.311265+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f89142b3ce3207a5f8a77e9d9fadf6b6d2e60a06c33b0f009a7d0dd0e6b49e25","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:quagmire of arXiv:2608.28505, 'Quagmires and large Suslin forests'] Given an uncountable cardinal $\kappa$ and a set $S \subseteq \mathrm{Lim}(\kappa)$, a\linebreak \emph{$(\kappa, S)$-quagmire} is a quadruple $(T, {<}, {\lhd}, Q)$ such that:
\begin{enumerate}[label={(Q\arabic*)},  start=0]
\item 
\begin{enumerate}
\item $(T, <)$ is a $\kappa$-Kurepa tree,
\item $\lhd$ is a binary relation on $T$ whose restriction to each level of $T$ is a strict linear order; nodes of distinct heights are $\lhd$-incomparable,
\item the function $Q$ is a partial function from $T^2$ to $T$ whose domain consists of the pairs $(x, y) \in T^2$ such that $\mathrm{ht}(x) < \mathrm{ht}(y)$ and $x \lhd \pi_{\mathrm{ht}(x)}(y)$,
\end{enumerate}

\item if $(x, y) \in \mathrm{dom}(Q)$, then $x < Q(x, y) \lhd y$,
\item if $(x, y) \in \mathrm{dom}(Q)$ and $y < z$, then $Q(Q(x, y), z) = Q(x,z)$,
\item if $(y, z) \in \mathrm{dom}(Q)$ and $x \lhd y$, then $Q(x, Q(y, z)) = Q(x, z)$,
\item if $x \lhd y$ and $\mathrm{ht}(x) \in S \cup \{\kappa\}$, then there exists $\alpha < \mathrm{ht}(x)$ such that $\pi_\alpha(x) \lhd \pi_\alpha(y)$ and $x = Q(\pi_\alpha(x), y)$.
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:51:00.246704+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f8b9f23362b53970696ce02831ac6517f5e6b45ed089ffb6889e42c3b7f28d64","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:REA of arXiv:2604.23981, 'Accelerating sampling via asymptotic relaxation enhancing flows'] Consider a given flow $v$. Let
$\sigma:=\liminf_{A\to\infty}\Psi_A$. Then,
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item $v$ is relaxation enhancing (or $\dot{\mathcal{I}}(v)=\emptyset$)
if and only if $\sigma=\infty$, and also if and only if $\lim_{A\to\infty}m_A=\infty$.

\item  If $\sigma<\infty$, then $\dot{\mathcal{I}}(v)$
is nonempty and 
\begin{gather}
\sigma=\lim_{A\to\infty}m_A=r(v).
\end{gather}
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, suppose $\sigma<\infty$ and $q_0$ satisfies Assumption (ass:warmstart of the paper) with $q_0-1\in \mathcal{Y}$. Then, for any $\delta>0$, there is some $A_0$ such that whenever $A>A_0$, one has
\[
\mathcal{H}(\rho(t)| \pi)=\int q \log q \pi dx \le C\int |h|^2\pi \,dx \le C_1\exp(-(\sigma-\delta) t),
\]
where $C_1$ depends only on the two constants in Assumption (ass:warmstart of the paper).","status":"unverified"}

\[
\boxed{\theta_i\le 2\alpha\qquad(1\le i\le n-1).}
\]
Equality holds exactly when $y_i=0$, equivalently $\psi_i=0$.
Conversely, given arbitrary turning angles $\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_{n-1}\in(0,\pi)$, every
\[
\alpha\in\left[\frac12\max_i\theta_i,\frac\pi2\right)
\]
occurs as the acute helix angle of some non-orthogonal discrete general helix with those turning angles and suitable torsion angles. Thus the turning-angle sequence alone imposes no further compatibility condition; the right panel of Figure~\ref{fig:phase-parametrisation} displays the bound and its equality case. If the lower endpoint $\alpha=\frac12\max_i\theta_i$ is chosen and all turning angles are equal, then all $\psi_i=0$, hence all $\phi_i=\pi$; this is exactly the alternating planar overlap described in Remark~\ref{rem:branch-overlap}.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:52:51.757105+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f8d6783728d74b3758ce08483a909446659b5f98b8ad6ef7da5a5eda5be0e804","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Dfs df0 of arXiv:2604.24061, 'A characterization of ruin-inducing probability measures in a renewal risk model'] \normalfont
		Let $Q$ be a probability measure on $(\varOmega,\varSigma)$.   \smallskip
		
		\noindent\textbf{(a)} If $\mathcal G{\,\subseteq\,}\varSigma$ is a $\sigma$-algebra of subsets of $\varOmega$, then  $Q$ is \textit{absolutely continuous}  with respect to $P$ on $\mathcal G$ (in symbols $Q{\upharpoonright}\mathcal G{\,\ll\,}P{\upharpoonright}\mathcal G$) if
		\[
		\forall\; A\in\mathcal G\quad  \Big( P(A)=0\Rightarrow Q(A)=0 \Big).
		\] 
		In addition, if $P{\upharpoonright}\mathcal G{\,\ll\,} Q{\upharpoonright}\mathcal G$, then $Q$ and $P$ are \textit{equivalent} on $\mathcal G$ (in symbols $Q{\upharpoonright}\mathcal G{\,\sim\,}P{\upharpoonright}\mathcal G$). For $\mathcal G{\,=\,}\varSigma$ simply write $Q{\,\ll\,} P$ and $Q{\sim}P$.  
		\smallskip
		
		\noindent  	\textbf{(b)} If $\{\mathcal G_t\}_{t\in\mathbb R_+}$ is a filtration for $\varSigma$, then $Q$ and $P$ are \textit{progressively equivalent} on $\{\mathcal G_t\}_{t\in\mathbb R_+}$, if $Q$ and $P$   are equivalent on each  $\mathcal G_t$ (i.e., $Q{\upharpoonright}\mathcal G_t{\,\sim\,} P{\upharpoonright}\mathcal G_t$). If $P$ and $Q$  are progressively equivalent with respect to $\{\mathcal G_t\}_{t\in\mathbb R_+}$, we write
		\[
		\frac{dQ}{dP}{\upharpoonright}\mathcal G_t:=\frac{d(Q{\upharpoonright}\mathcal G_t)}{d(P{\upharpoonright}\mathcal G_t)} \,\,\text{ for all }  t\in\mathbb R_+
		\]
		for simplicity.","status":"unverified"}

\bel{eq:pot-relax-map}

\zeta_{\alpha\beta}\mathscr B^{\alpha\beta}(\beta,\zeta)\geq0,

\zeta_{\alpha\beta}\mathscr B^{\alpha\beta}(\beta,\zeta)=0

\bel{eq:pot-relax-linearization}

\eta_{\alpha\beta}\mathbb M^{\alpha\beta\gamma\delta}(\beta)\eta_{\gamma\delta}>0

\ee

\ee","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["(a_n)_{n >= 0} is a real sequence","the second differences a_n - 2a_{n+1} + a_{n+2} are nonnegative for every n >= 0 (convexity)","a_n -> 0 as n -> infinity","consequences used and derived from these: a_n >= 0, a_n nonincreasing, n(a_n - a_{n+1}) -> 0, sum (n+1)(a_n - 2a_{n+1} + a_{n+2}) = a_0","integrability is with respect to Lebesgue measure on the circle"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T19:07:38.815245+00:00","domain":"Fourier analysis, trigonometric series","id":"claim_f95cf78453cad9016df951c8497b0e8bcbb54049fe66f88a10ab868d7db99aa2","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let (a_n)_{n >= 0} be real numbers which are CONVEX, meaning the second differences D2 a_n := a_n - 2 a_{n+1} + a_{n+2} are >= 0 for every n >= 0, and which tend to 0. (These two hypotheses already force a_n >= 0 and a_n nonincreasing: the first differences a_{n+1} - a_n are nondecreasing, so if one of them were positive the sequence would tend to +infinity. They also force n(a_n - a_{n+1}) -> 0, since the differences are monotone.) THEOREM (Young; Zygmund, Trigonometric Series, Ch. V). Put S(x) = a_0/2 + sum_{n >= 1} a_n cos(nx). Then: (1) the series converges for every x not in 2 pi Z, uniformly on every compact subset of (0, 2 pi); (2) S(x) >= 0 for all such x; (3) S is Lebesgue integrable on (-pi, pi), with (1/(2 pi)) times the integral of S over (-pi,pi) equal to a_0/2; (4) the series IS the Fourier series of S, that is a_n = (1/pi) times the integral over (-pi,pi) of S(x) cos(nx) dx for every n >= 0. The whole theorem rests on one identity: with K_n(x) = (1/(n+1)) (sin((n+1)x/2) / sin(x/2))^2 >= 0 the Fejer kernel, normalised so that (1/(2 pi)) times the integral of K_n over (-pi,pi) is 1, double summation by parts gives S(x) = sum_{n >= 0} (n+1) (D2 a_n) (1/2) K_n(x), with sum_{n >= 0} (n+1) D2 a_n = a_0 < infinity. Nonnegativity is then read off from D2 a_n >= 0 and K_n >= 0, and integrability from the normalisation. SHARP EDGES. (a) It is CONVEXITY, not monotone decrease, that does the work: monotone decrease to zero gives convergence off the origin by Dirichlet's test, but it does not produce the Fejer representation and therefore gives neither nonnegativity nor integrability of the sum. (b) The SINE analogue is false in this form. If (b_n) is convex and decreases to 0, then sum b_n sin(nx) still converges pointwise off 2 pi Z, but its sum is Lebesgue integrable if and only if sum b_n / n converges. The classical counterexample is b_n = 1/log n for n >= 2, which is convex and decreases to 0 while sum 1/(n log n) diverges: the resulting series converges everywhere but is not the Fourier series of any Lebesgue integrable function. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:34:33.545854+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f986deb0243b0fdeb46824059e927a217b9dd4adfc062cb50b1c5255b34023da","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 56 (Villain model) of arXiv:2603.28734, 'Free energy analyticity of the disordered XY model and Debye screening in the 2D Coulomb g'] Fix $d\in\Z_{\geq 1}$ and $\beta\in\R_{\geq 0}$.
    For any domain $\Lambda$ and $\zeta:\Z^d\to\S^1$,
    the \emph{Villain model} on $\Lambda$ with boundary condition $\zeta$
    at inverse temperature $\beta$ is the probability measure  on $\sigma\in(\S^1)^\Lambda$ given by
    \[
        \diff\mu_{\Villain,\Lambda,\beta}^\zeta(\sigma) = \frac1{Z_{\Villain,\Lambda,\beta}^\zeta} e^{-H_{\Villain,\Lambda,\beta}^\zeta(\sigma)} \diff\sigma,
    \]
    where $Z_{\Villain,\Lambda,\beta}^\zeta$ is the normalising constant,
    $\diff\sigma$ the Haar measure, and
    \begin{multline}
         e^{-H_{\Villain,\Lambda,\beta}^\zeta(\sigma)}
         =
         \Big(\prod_{\substack{\{x,y\}\subset\Lambda\\x\sim y}}p_\beta(\sigma_x,\sigma_y)\Big)
            \Big(\prod_{\substack{x\in\Lambda,\,y\in\Lambda^c\\x\sim y}}p_\beta(\sigma_x,\zeta_y)\Big);
            \\
         p_\beta(z,z'):=\sum_{m\in\Z} e^{-\frac{\beta}{2}\big(\arg(z)-\arg(z')+2\pi m\big)^2}.
    \end{multline}
    Notice that the Hamiltonian is defined somewhat atypically and incorporates
    the dependency on $\beta$; more on this later.
    The \emph{critical inverse temperature} is defined as the largest $\beta_c^{\Villain}=\beta_c^{\Villain}(d)\in(0,\infty)$
    such that $\mu_{\Villain,\Lambda_n,\beta}^{+1}[\sigma_0]$ decays exponentially fast in $n$
    for any fixed $\beta\in[0,\beta_c^{\Villain})$.
    Classical arguments based on correlations inequalities imply the existence of an infinite-volume Gibbs measure with $+1$ boundary conditions at inverse temperature $\beta\geq 0$, that we refer to as $\mu^{+1}_{\Villain, \beta}$.
    The label $\Villain$ is omitted from notations when it is clear from the context.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:53:10.207321+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f9d0739d9e23ab53e239f28ab875855eaf9b4d07e87c68393341a2de9cc9aac1","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defi Def:Bary-Subdiv-Weighted of arXiv:2608.29013, 'Weighted Homology and Cohomology of Weighted Polyhedra'] \ \vskip 0.1cm
 For a weighted simplicial complex $(K,\mu)$, define the weight of the barycenter $b_{\sigma}$ of any simplex $\sigma$ in $K$ to be $\mu(\sigma)$. Then define a weight  $Sd(\mu)$ on $Sd(K)$ by:
    \begin{equation} 
     Sd(\mu)\big([ b_{\sigma_0},\cdots, b_{\sigma_l}]\big)=\mu(\sigma_l),\ \sigma_0\subsetneq \cdots\subsetneq \sigma_l \in K.
     \end{equation}
   
   Note that we have either
   $\mu(\sigma_0)\, | \, \cdots \, | \,\mu(\sigma_l)$ or 
    $\mu(\sigma_l) \, |\, \cdots\, |\, \mu(\sigma_0)$ depending on whether $\mu$ is ascending or descending. Then it is easy to 
    check that $Sd(\mu)$ is a divisible weight on $Sd(K)$ which is ascending (or descending) if so is $\mu$.  
     We call $(Sd(K),Sd(\mu))$ the \emph{barycentric subdivision} of $(K,\mu)$. For any integer $m\geqslant 1$, let $(Sd^m(K),Sd^m(\mu))$ 
 denote the $m$ iterated barycentric subdivisions of $(K,\mu)$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T11:07:35.014292+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f9f11b2cef699280406131b0616cabc55e67dab81fb1661a6541cc44001fcfc3","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 6 of arXiv:2609.02878, '2609.02878'] A \emph{limiting point} at time \(T\) is an element
\(\xi\in M_T\) of Bamler's metric-flow slice at the limiting time
\cite[Definition~2.32 and the paragraph following
equation~(2.34)]{BamlerStructure}.  We represent it by a probability
conjugate heat flow
\[
 \xi=(\mu_t)_{t<T},\qquad d\mu_t=v_t\,dV_{g(t)},
\]
where
\[
 \partial_tv_t=-\Delta_{g(t)}v_t+R_{g(t)}v_t,
 \qquad v_t>0,
 \qquad \int_Xv_t\,dV_{g(t)}=1.
\]
The representation has the following two properties of the limiting slice:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(P\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item \(\xi\) is a subsequential limit of point conjugate heat flows
whose pole times increase to \(T\);
\item for \(D=2n\),
\begin{equation}
 \Var_{g(t)}(\mu_t)
 :=\iint_{X\times X}d_{g(t)}(x,y)^2\,d\mu_t(x)d\mu_t(y)
 \le H_{2n}(T-t).
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
The limiting point is called \emph{fixed} when it is chosen before any
sequence of blow-up scales.  Every tangent argument below keeps this
same limiting point while the scales vary.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["an i.i.d., or ergodic and suitably mixing, random environment","a directional transience condition, typically Sznitman's (T) or (T'), or an equivalent ballisticity condition, in some direction l","uniform ellipticity of the transition probabilities, standard though sometimes relaxed in specific results","existence of well-defined regeneration times with positive probability of never backtracking, verified from the environment's independence or mixing structure"],"created_at":"2026-09-07T08:44:20.988973+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f9f2aaae6b2438ff5a64f4f66dc265aa11c167d9a714a9526edfe927fb576ab3","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). For random walk in a random environment on Z^d satisfying a directional transience condition, such as Sznitman's condition (T) or the stronger (T') in a direction l, or a simpler ballisticity/non-nestling condition, one constructs regeneration times tau_1 < tau_2 < ... at which the walk achieves a new running maximum in direction l and never backtracks below that level afterward. Under condition (T'), or the weaker (T), the increments (X_{tau_{k+1}} - X_{tau_k}, tau_{k+1} - tau_k), for k >= 1, form an i.i.d. sequence, reducing the walk, which is not itself Markovian once the environment is averaged out, to a genuine i.i.d.-increment structure from which a law of large numbers (a deterministic limiting velocity) follows directly, and, with additional finite-moment control on the regeneration increments, a central limit theorem follows via classical tools for sums of i.i.d. variables. This does not establish the directional transience condition itself, verifying (T) or (T') for a given environment law is typically the hard remaining step; it does not directly give a central limit theorem without separately checking finite second moments of the regeneration increments, which can genuinely fail in slow or near-critical regimes; and it is specific to the static, fixed-in-time environment model. Typical failure: Assuming the regeneration increments automatically have finite variance, and hence a central limit theorem follows, once ballisticity or condition (T') has been established; ballisticity under (T') only guarantees a finite mean regeneration time, and a genuine central limit theorem requires an additional, often delicate, verification of finite second moments, a point on which the Kesten-Kozlov-Spitzer branching-with-migration machinery exists precisely because these moments can fail. Canonical reference: Sznitman and Zerner, 1999, Annals of Probability; Sznitman, 2002, Ecole d'Ete de Probabilites de Saint-Flour, Springer Lecture Notes in Mathematics.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:34:33.543019+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fa18f25af7b7b7bf663f7e66579a87c2a4d4c15e3c11603a7ee5fb076d7082d4","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 19 (The models are EFIIDs) of arXiv:2603.28734, 'Free energy analyticity of the disordered XY model and Debye screening in the 2D Coulomb g'] All three models alluded to above are EFIIDs.
    More precisely, we obtain the following results.
    \begin{itemize}
        \item[\emph{\textbf{XY}}] Consider the XY model in dimension $d\in\Z_{\geq 2}$
        at inverse temperature $\beta\in[0,\beta_c(d))$.
        Then the infinite-volume Gibbs measure $\mu_{\XY,\beta}^{+1}$
        is an EFIID.
        \item[\emph{\textbf{SWM}}] Consider the SWM in dimension $d\in\Z_{\geq 2}$
        at inverse temperature $\beta\in\R_{\geq 0}$.
        Then the infinite-volume Gibbs measure $\mu_{\SWM,\beta}^0$
        is an EFIID.
        \item[\emph{\textbf{Coulomb}}] Consider the two-dimensional Coulomb gas at $\beta\in[0,\beta_{\BKT}(\Villain))$.
        Then the sequence $(\mu_{\Coulomb,\Lambda_n,\beta}^\free)_n$
        tends to some infinite-volume measure $\mu_{\Coulomb,\beta}^\free$ on $\Z^{F(\Z^2)}$ as $n\to\infty$ in the local convergence topology,
        and this limit is an EFIID.
    \end{itemize}
    In the case of the Coulomb gas, we are careful not to call this measure a Gibbs measure, as the Hamiltonian of the model is non-local and therefore it is not so clear what it means exactly to be a Gibbs measure.

    In particular, these results imply that for any of the three models,
    correlations between bounded observables decay exponentially fast in the distance at which they are measured. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:26:47.190930+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fa474a8a4624814fe97709dafbef801fb0755ea4276210b20d5a5f868b3d8f3d","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem 109 (regularity for spatially smoothed coefficients) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] The coefficients from Definition~\ref{d:sp.smooth} are continuously differentiable in the space coordinate, and satisfy the bounds
	\[
	\Big(
	\|\sB^N\|_\infty
    +
    \|\partial_y\sB^N\|_\infty\Big)^2
	+ \max\bigg\{
    \|\tilde{A}\|_\infty
    +\|\partial_y\tilde{A}\|_\infty
    : \tilde{A}\in\{ \sV,\sU,\srrr,\swww\}^N
    \bigg\}
	\le 
	\bigg(\frac{\trK L}{\sep}\bigg)^{O(1)} 
	(\MAX_N)^2\,,
	\]
with $\MAX_N$ as in \eqref{e:MAX.N} and Proposition~\ref{p:Y.kolmogorov}.

\begin{proof}
We continue to use the abbreviations introduced above. To simplify notation, we mostly suppress the dependence on $N$ inside the proof. Consider
	\[
	\sB(t,y)
	=\frac{\overline{\varrho_{D,t}*\sphi}(y)}
		{\overline{\varrho_t*\sphi}(y)}
	\equiv \frac{\Num(t,y)}{\Den(t,y)}\,.
	\]
We first aim to lower bound the denominator $\Den$.
Recall from Definition~\ref{d:sp.smooth} that $\sphi$ has support $[-\sep,\sep]^3$, and is $\ge \Omega(1)/\sep^3$ on $[-\sep/2,\sep/2]^3$. 
From the construction of $\vX^\frozen$ and $\vY^\frozen$
(Definitions \ref{d:trunc}--\ref{d:rerand.Ising}), we see that $\varrho_t$ gives measure at least $\Omega( \sep^3 /\trK^{O(1)} )$ to any box of side length $\sep$ contained in $[-2\trK,2\trK]^3$. It follows that, for all $\vy\in[-2\trK+1,2\trK-1]^3$,
	\[
	\varrho_t*\sphi(\vy)
	\ge \int_{[-\sep/2,\sep/2]^3}
		\sphi(\vy-\vx)\,\varrho_t(d\vx)
	\ge \frac{1}{\trK^{O(1)}}\,.
	\]
Integrating over $\vy\in H(y)$ (as defined by \eqref{e:hspace.y}) gives
	\beq
	\Den(t,y)
	= \overline{\varrho_t*\sphi}(y)
	\ge \frac{1}{\trK^{O(1)}}
	\eeq
for all $y\in[-5\trK,5\trK]$. Next note that since particles outside $[-\trK,\trK]^3$ are frozen (see Definition~\ref{d:trunc}), the numerator $\Num(t,y)$ must be zero for $y\notin[-3\trK-1,3\trK+1]$. For $y\in[-3\trK-1,3\trK+1]$, we bound
	\begin{align*}
	|\Num(t,y)|
	&=\Big|\overline{\varrho_{D,t}*\sphi}(y)\Big|
	=\bigg| \int_{H(y)}
	\int_{\R^3} \sphi(\vy-\vx)B(t,\vx)\,\varrho_t(d\vx) \,d\vy\bigg|\\
	&=\bigg| \int_{\R^3}
	B(t,\vx) \overline{\sphi}(y-(\underline{1},\vx))\,\varrho_t(d\vx)\bigg|
	\le \|\overline{\sphi}\|_\infty \cdot \int_{\R^3}
	|B(t,\vx)|\,\varrho_t(d\vx)
	\le  \bigg(\frac{L}
		{\sep}\bigg)^{O(1)}
		\MAX_N\,,
	\end{align*}
where the last step uses the quenched moment bound on $\bbb$ from Lemma~\ref{l:barD.I.second.quenched}, together with the bound $(p^N)' \le  L^2$ from \eqref{e:sdelimits.pprime}. Combining with \eqref{e:denominator.lbd} gives
	\[\|\sB\|_\infty 
	\le \bigg(\frac{\trK L}
		{\sep}
		\bigg)^{O(1)}
		\MAX_N\,.
	\]
We can also apply \eqref{e:denominator.lbd} to obtain
	\beq
	\Big|\partial_y \tilde{B}(t,y)\Big|
	\le \trK^{O(1)}
	\bigg|
	\frac{\partial}{\partial y} \Num(t,y)
	- \tilde{B}(t,y)
	\frac{\partial}{\partial y} \Den(t,y)
	\bigg|\,.\eeq
The first term on the right-hand side of \eqref{e:sB.quotient.rule} can be bounded by
	\begin{align*}
	\bigg|\frac{\partial}{\partial y} \Num(t,y)\bigg|
	&=\bigg|\frac{\partial}{\partial y}
	\overline{\varrho_{D,t}*\sphi}(y)\bigg|
	=\bigg| 
	\int_{\R^3} B(t,\vx)
	\overline{\sphi}' (y-(\vec{1},\vx))
	\,\varrho_t(d\vx)
	\bigg|\\
	&\le
	\|\overline{\sphi}' \|_\infty
	\int_{\R^3} | B(t,\vx) | \,\varrho_t(d\vx)
	\le \bigg(\frac{L}
		{\sep}\bigg)^{O(1)} \MAX_N\,.
	\end{align*}
The second term on the right-hand side of \eqref{e:sB.quotient.rule} can be controlled using the preceding bound on $\tilde{B}$, together with a similar  calculation as above:
	\[
	\bigg|\frac{\partial}{\partial y}
		\Den(t,y) \bigg|
	=\bigg|\frac{\partial}{\partial y}
	\overline{\varrho_t*\sphi}(y)\bigg|
	\le  \| \overline{\sphi}' \|_\infty \cdot
	\int_{\R^3} \varrho_t(d\vx)
	\le \frac{1}{\sep^{O(1)} }\,.
	\]
Combining the above gives the claimed bound on $\partial_y \sB$.
The bounds on $\sV$, $\sU$, $\srrr$, and $\swww$ follow by the same argument, using the quenched moment bounds from Lemma~\ref{l:tQ.first.quenched}.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:54:34.576894+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fa483578692ebb64fd65c90d7dd282dc4a175130c5fa82aad1ee8b96558013a2","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Prop 10 of arXiv:2606.14812, 'Joint convergence in Wiener chaos via transport hierarchy and Malliavin covariances'] Consider two integers $p, q\geq 2$ and let
		\[
		X_N = I_p(f_N), \qquad Y_N = I_q(g_N),
		\]
		where $f_N\in H^{\odot p}$, $g_N\in H^{\odot q}$, and assume that $X_N$ 
		satisfies \eqref{c1} and $Y_N$ is bounded in $L^2(\Omega)$. Write 
		$q = ap + r'$ with $a\geq 1$ and $0\leq r' < p$. For $r\geq 1$, let 
		$Y_{r,N}$ be given by \eqref{yr}. Then the following hold.
		
		\begin{enumerate}
			\item For every integer $r\geq 1$ with $rp\leq q$,
			\begin{equation}
				Y_{r,N} = C_{r,p,q}\,
				I_{q-rp}\!\left(f_N\widetilde\otimes_p^{(r)} g_N\right)
				+ R_{r,N},
			\end{equation}
			where $f_N\widetilde\otimes_p^{(r)} g_N$ denotes the 
			$r$-fold iterated contraction of $f_N$ with $g_N$, 
			defined recursively by $f_N\widetilde\otimes_p^{(1)} g_N 
			= f_N\widetilde\otimes_p g_N\in H^{\odot(q-p)}$ and
			\begin{equation*}
				f_N\widetilde\otimes_p^{(r)} g_N 
				:= f_N\widetilde\otimes_p 
				\left(f_N\widetilde\otimes_p^{(r-1)} g_N\right)
				\in H^{\odot(q-rp)},
				\quad r=2,\ldots,a,
			\end{equation*}
			i.e.\ at each step the $p$ variables of $f_N$ are 
			fully contracted with $p$ of the remaining variables 
			of the kernel from the previous step. Also,  $C_{r,p,q} = (p!)^r\frac{q!}{(q-rp)!}$ and 
			$R_{r,N}\to 0$ in $L^2(\Omega)$ as $N\to\infty$.
			
			\item \textbf{Non-critical case} $ap < q < (a+1)p$: 
			\begin{equation}
				Y_{a+1,N} \to _{N \to \infty}0 \quad \text{in } L^2(\Omega).
			\end{equation}
			
			\item \textbf{Critical case} $q = ap$: taking $r=a$ in \eqref{14m-2b} gives
			\begin{equation*}
				Y_{a,N} - \mathbf{E}[Y_{a,N}] \to  _{N \to \infty}0 \quad \text{in } L^2(\Omega).
			\end{equation*}
			In particular, if $\mathbf{E}[Y_{a,N}]\to _{N \to \infty}\rho_a$ for some $\rho_a\in\mathbb{R}$, 
			then $Y_{a,N}\to _{N \to \infty}\rho_a$ in $L^2(\Omega)$. Moreover,
			\begin{equation}
				Y_{a+1,N} \to_{N \to \infty}  0 \quad \text{in } L^2(\Omega).
			\end{equation}
		\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:53:00.840427+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fa4e56c3bebc9282e6444314924ed85ae271b67a30e98fb1b6f56449b0d0585c","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition Def: reduction steps of arXiv:2607.18635, 'Remainders of generalised Taylor expansions and a priori bounds for rough differential equ'] Given $\rho\in{\mathcal T}_b^{I_k}$ we fix a reduction chain $(\rho^0,\rho^1,\ldots,\rho^k)$ of $\rho$ as in Definition (Def: reduction chain of the paper).

{"assumptions":["G = PSL(2,R) and Gamma < G is discrete with finite covolume (a lattice)","m is the G-invariant probability measure on Gamma\\G","the flow is right translation by the one-parameter unipotent subgroup u_t","no cocompactness, torsion freeness or arithmeticity is assumed for (1)-(3); cocompactness is needed only for minimality and unique ergodicity, which are NOT claimed here","mixing is understood with respect to the normalised invariant probability measure"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T19:20:07.090417+00:00","domain":"homogeneous dynamics, unipotent flows, mixing","id":"claim_fa58123752f92f96ece864fcf1e4a8975e90b2041eda5d1899f3190c01222269","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let G = PSL(2,R) and let Gamma be a LATTICE in G: a discrete subgroup such that the quotient M = Gamma\\G carries a G-invariant Borel probability measure m (finite covolume, normalised). Gamma is not assumed torsion free, cocompact, or arithmetic. For real t let u_t denote the image in G of the unipotent matrix with rows (1, t) and (0, 1), and define the horocycle flow on M by h_t(Gamma g) = Gamma g u_t. Then: (1) each h_t preserves m; (2) HEDLUND: the flow is ergodic with respect to m; (3) PARRY: the flow is strongly mixing, that is for all F1, F2 in L^2(M, m) the inner product of F1 composed with h_t against F2 converges, as |t| -> infinity, to the product of the integral of F1 and the conjugate of the integral of F2; equivalently m(A intersect h_{-t}B) -> m(A) m(B) for all Borel A, B. Moreover the flow is mixing of all orders. WHERE THE HYPOTHESES BITE: (i) finite covolume is essential. Mixing as stated is a statement about a probability measure; for a discrete subgroup of infinite covolume the correct statements concern Burger-Roblin and Patterson-Sullivan measures and carry extra hypotheses (for instance on the critical exponent), so (3) must not be quoted there. (ii) Ergodicity and mixing hold for EVERY lattice, but MINIMALITY (every orbit dense), Hedlund's other theorem, needs Gamma cocompact: a noncompact finite-volume quotient has closed horocycle orbits encircling each cusp, so the flow there is mixing yet neither minimal nor uniquely ergodic. Confusing the two Hedlund statements is the usual error. (iii) The result concerns the unipotent direction. The geodesic flow a_s is also mixing but has positive entropy and a huge simplex of invariant measures, whereas the horocycle flow has zero entropy and (in the cocompact case) is uniquely ergodic; rigidity statements do not transfer between them. (iv) Nothing here gives a RATE; quantitative mixing needs a spectral gap input and the rate depends on the lattice.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T11:26:52.675062+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fa97832749f5ba14f0a0a6e7f2aefbd508f15a7765b318b44d9e160b783f671e","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 7 of arXiv:2609.03750, '\bf Pullback Measure Attractors, Zero-Noise Limits, and Moderate Deviations for 2D Stochas'] Let
		\[
		S(t,\tau):\mathcal P_{4,z}(H)\longrightarrow
		\mathcal P_{4,z}(H),\qquad t\geq\tau,
		\]
		be a measure evolution process satisfying
		\[
		S(\tau,\tau)=I,\qquad
		S(t,s)S(s,\tau)=S(t,\tau),
		\quad t\geq s\geq\tau.
		\]
		A family
		$\mathscr A=\{\mathscr A(\tau):\tau\in\mathbb R\}
		\in\mathfrak D$
		is called a $\mathfrak D$-pullback measure attractor for $S$ if:
		\begin{enumerate}
			\item[(1)] for every $\tau\in\mathbb R$, the set
			$\mathscr A(\tau)$ is nonempty and compact in
			$(\mathcal P(H),d_{\mathcal P(H)})$;
			
			\item[(2)] $\mathscr A$ is invariant, namely,
			\[
			S(t,\tau)\mathscr A(\tau)=\mathscr A(t),
			\qquad t\geq\tau;
			\]
			
			\item[(3)] $\mathscr A$ pullback attracts every $D\in\mathfrak D$,
			that is, for every $\tau\in\mathbb R$,
			\[
			\lim_{r\to\infty}
			\operatorname{dist}_{w,H}
			\bigl(
			S(\tau,\tau-r)D(\tau-r),
			\mathscr A(\tau)
			\bigr)=0.
			\]
		\end{enumerate}
		Here compactness and attraction are understood in the weak topology
		of probability measures on $H$, while membership in $\mathfrak D$
		retains the fourth-order and vertical-derivative moments required
		to restart the equation.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:25:06.135376+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fa9a803be9844db7375f91bafd050fc295e46c3963d12076c7e010859ee4da39","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Thm 2 of arXiv:2608.22514, 'Diffusion limits of cyclic finite-velocity random motions\\ along vector fields'] Suppose that assumptions
$\mathbf{A}_V$,
$\mathbf{A}_\tau$,
$\mathbf{A}_{V,\mu}$ and
$\mathbf{A}_\varkappa$ hold. Then, for any initial values $y\in\bR^d$ and $\iota\in \{1,\dots,p\}$,
the gliding evolutions $\{Y^{\e,\delta}\}$ converge weakly in $C(\bR_+,\bR^d)$
to a diffusion $Y$ starting at $y$ with the generator
\ba

Bf
&=\frac{\varkappa^2}{2\mu} \sum_{i}  \sigma_{i}^2  \langle \nabla^2 f V_i ,V_i\rangle
+ \frac{\varkappa^2}{2\mu}\sum_{i} \lambda_{i}^2 \langle \nabla f, DV_i[V_i]\rangle
+\frac{\varkappa^2}{\mu}\sum_{j<i} \mu_i\mu_j \langle \nabla f, DV_i[V_j] \rangle
,\quad f\in C^3_b(\bR^d,\bR).
\ea
The diffusion $Y$ is a solution to an It\^o-SDE
\ba

\di Y_t= \frac{\varkappa}{\sqrt\mu}  \sum_{i} \sigma_{i} V_i(Y_t)\,\di W^i_t +
\frac{\varkappa^2}{\mu} \Big(
\frac12\sum_{i} \lambda_{i}^2 DV_i[V_i](Y_t)
+\sum_{j< i} \mu_i\mu_j  D V_i [ V_j](Y_t)
\Big)\,\di t,
\ea
where $W^1,\dots,W^p$ are independent standard one-dimensional Brownian motions.
The SDE \eqref{e:SDEY} can be rewritten in the Stratonovich form
as
\ba

\di Y_t= \frac{\varkappa}{\sqrt\mu}  \sum_{i} \sigma_{i} V_i(Y_t)\circ\di W^i_t
+\frac{\varkappa^2}{2\mu} \sum_{j< i} \mu_i\mu_j  [ V_i,V_j](Y_t)\,\di t.
\ea (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:06:21.667881+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_faa9705b72fd293bd94ec319bd953d1b7fca22e4fb16d94f7e81c486d6f2200b","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 1 of arXiv:2607.20838, 'Long-memory Markov chains with power-law intensities'] Let $\{ \varepsilon_n \}_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of independent and identically distributed random variables. 
	Suppose there exists a stochastic process $\{ \mathbf{X}_n \}$ taking values in $\mathbb{R}^d$ for some $d \ge 1$, which governs the distribution of inter-arrival times $\{ \tau_n \}$.
	Let \(\Phi(t,\mathbf{x})\) be a function defined for \(t \ge 0\) and \(\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^d\), and assume that \(\Phi(\cdot,\mathbf{x})\) is strictly increasing in \(t\) for each fixed \(\mathbf{x}\).
	The inter-arrival time \(\tau_n\) is related to \(\varepsilon_n\) by
	\begin{equation}
		\varepsilon_n = \Phi(\tau_n, \mathbf{X}_{n-1}) 
		\qquad \text{equivalently,} \qquad
		\tau_n = \Phi^{-1}(\varepsilon_n, \mathbf{X}_{n-1}) ,
		
	\end{equation}
	where the inverse is taken with respect to $t$, holding $\mathbf{x}$ fixed.
	The process $\mathbf{X}_n$ evolves according to an update function $\Psi$ such that
	\begin{equation}
		\mathbf{X}_n = \Psi(\mathbf{X}_{n-1}, \tau_n). 
	\end{equation}
	The associated point process \(N\) on \(\mathbb{R}^+\) is defined by
	\[
	N = \sum_{n \in \mathbb N} \delta_{T_n}, 
	\qquad  \qquad 
	T_n = \sum_{i=1}^n \tau_i
	\]
	where \(\delta_t\) denotes the Dirac measure at \(t\).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["H_k the Sylvester Hadamard matrix of order 2^k, disc(A) = min over sign vectors x of ||A x||_inf"],"created_at":"2026-09-24T23:46:59.335012+00:00","domain":"combinatorics/Boolean functions","id":"claim_face5f144efa4b4e9a635b179d81577f","kind":"counterexample","schema_version":1,"statement":"Conjecture 13 of the Randomstrasse 2024 problem list asks whether the Sylvester Hadamard matrix H_k of order 2^k has discrepancy disc(H_k) = sqrt(2) sqrt(2^k) for odd k, where disc(A) = min over sign vectors x of the sup-norm of Ax. In plain terms: take the 2^k x 2^k matrix of plus and minus ones whose entry in row a and column u is (-1) to the mod-2 dot product of the k-bit strings a and u, and ask for the smallest possible largest absolute entry of the product Hx over sign vectors x. Indexing H_k by (-1)^{a.u} and reading x as the +-1 truth table of a Boolean function f on k variables, H_k x is the Walsh transform W_f, so disc(H_k) = min_f max_a |W_f(a)| = 2^k - 2 NL_max(k), where NL_max(k) is the largest nonlinearity of a Boolean function on k variables (the covering radius of the Reed-Muller code RM(1, k)). The conjectured value is exactly the bent-concatenation bound NL = 2^{k-1} - 2^{(k-1)/2}, which is beaten for odd k = 15 (Patterson and Wiedemann, 1983) and for every odd k > 7 (Kavut, Maitra and Yucel, 2006), and is optimal for k <= 7. So the conjecture holds exactly for k in {1, 3, 5, 7} and fails for every odd k >= 9. The numbers: for k <= 7 the maximum nonlinearity equals the bent-concatenation value (the covering radius of RM(1,5) is 12, Berlekamp and Welch 1972; of RM(1,7) is 56, Mykkeltveit 1980; k = 1, 3 by hand); for k = 9 functions of nonlinearity 242 exist (Kavut, Maitra and Yucel 2006), so disc(H_9) <= 512 - 484 = 28 < 32; for every odd k = 9 + 2j the direct sum of such a function with a bent function on 2j variables has largest Walsh coefficient 28 * 2^j, below 32 * 2^j, since the Walsh spectrum of a direct sum is the product; and Patterson and Wiedemann's nonlinearity 16276 on 15 variables gives disc(H_15) <= 216 < 256.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["the point process is exactly determinantal, or Pfaffian with the analogous but distinct formula, with a well-defined correlation kernel K satisfying the standard positivity and boundedness conditions","the conditioning event is of the specific form covered by the Schur-complement formula, i.e. an exact configuration on a subset, or the corresponding L-ensemble conditioning","invertibility, or a well-defined limiting or pseudo-inverse procedure, for the relevant diagonal block appearing in the formula, e.g. K_AA - I","the block partition A, B is taken with respect to the same index set on which K is originally defined"],"created_at":"2026-09-07T08:44:20.998694+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_faf3e83a28894a41c1931704cf7a671a579f690c334933aa41076761cbab8d22","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). For a determinantal point process with correlation kernel K, Hermitian and satisfying 0<=K<=I in the discrete finite-space setting, the conditional law of the process restricted to a subset given the exact configuration on the complementary subset is again determinantal, with a kernel given by a Schur-complement formula. Partitioning the index set into A, the observed subset, and B, the remaining subset, and writing K in block form with entries K_AA, K_AB, K_BA, K_BB, the conditional kernel on B given the exact points observed in A is expressed via a Schur-complement expression such as K_BB - K_BA (K_AA - I)^{-1} K_AB, with the precise form depending on the convention used (correlation kernel versus L-ensemble) and on whether one conditions on points being present or absent in A. This identity is the fundamental tool for analyzing conditioning, dynamics, and Gibbs-type properties of determinantal processes, including eigenvalues of random matrices, non-intersecting paths, discrete orthogonal polynomial ensembles, and, via the transfer-current theorem, uniform spanning trees, reducing conditional analysis to linear algebra on the kernel matrix. It does not apply outside the determinantal class of point processes, or its Pfaffian analogue for orthogonal and symplectic ensembles, which has a related but distinct formula, and the exact form of the Schur complement depends sensitively on the specific conditioning event and on invertibility of the relevant block, which can fail or require a pseudo-inverse or limiting argument at special parameter values. Typical failure: Applying a Schur-complement conditional-kernel formula derived under one convention, such as conditioning an L-ensemble on a fixed exact sample, to a different conditioning question, such as conditioning on a sub-event like at least one point in a region, or mixing up the correlation-kernel and L-ensemble conventions, without re-deriving the correct formula; determinantal-process conditioning identities are convention-sensitive, and mixing them up produces a kernel that still looks plausible, expressed via some Schur complement, but does not correctly describe the actual conditional process. Canonical reference: Shirai and Takahashi, 2003, Journal of Functional Analysis; Borodin and Rains, 2005, Journal of Statistical Physics; Lyons, 2003, Annals of Probability.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:33:12.355668+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fb4c25432ee016755b79aa49443148782cd3f00e8d745823c6c72b7fc454ea99","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Thm 225 (\textbf{main result}) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For the spherical projection pursuit problem \eqref{eq:proj-pursuit-def}, we have the following:
    \begin{enumerate}[(a)]
        \item

        \item 
        
        For any $\fq \in [1,2)$ and $\iotamsr > 0$, there exists small $\iotasol > 0$ such that the following holds.

{"assumptions":["f is Lebesgue integrable on R^d","convention: kernel e^{-2 pi i x.xi} with no normalizing constant"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:49:39.261959+00:00","domain":"harmonic analysis on Euclidean space","id":"claim_fb60e476216b9503fe6cf25758a518637c753a94a69a4d29f3d7163257a33360","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"For $f \\in L^1(\\mathbb{R}^d)$ define $\\hat f(\\xi) = \\int_{\\mathbb{R}^d} f(x) e^{-2\\pi i x\\cdot\\xi}\\,dx$ for every $\\xi \\in \\mathbb{R}^d$; the integral converges absolutely for every $\\xi$. The map $f\\mapsto\\hat f$ is linear, $\\hat f$ is bounded and uniformly continuous, and $\\|\\hat f\\|_\\infty \\le \\|f\\|_1$. Symmetry rules (for $a,b\\in\\mathbb{R}^d$, $\\lambda>0$): $x\\mapsto f(x-a)$ has transform $e^{-2\\pi i a\\cdot\\xi}\\hat f(\\xi)$; $x\\mapsto e^{2\\pi i b\\cdot x}f(x)$ has transform $\\hat f(\\xi-b)$; $x\\mapsto f(\\lambda x)$ has transform $\\lambda^{-d}\\hat f(\\xi/\\lambda)$; $\\overline f$ has transform $\\overline{\\hat f(-\\xi)}$. The inverse transform of $g\\in L^1$ is $\\check g(x)=\\int g(\\xi)e^{2\\pi i x\\cdot\\xi}\\,d\\xi$. With this convention Plancherel reads $\\|\\hat f\\|_2=\\|f\\|_2$. Convention warning: texts using $\\int f(x)e^{-ix\\cdot\\xi}dx$ have inversion with a factor $(2\\pi)^{-d}$ and $\\|\\hat f\\|_2=(2\\pi)^{d/2}\\|f\\|_2$; the unitary convention puts $(2\\pi)^{-d/2}$ in front of both. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:17:04.323197+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fb698b50b917460bf07b1c0ecb9d62b64257a4d56f8333f426c1cdf0533aecc3","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma Lemma 4.1 in sethuraman-varadhan of arXiv:2606.01683, 'Singular-value gap of nonreversible Markov processes'] Let $S$ be a standard Borel space, $Q$ a probability measure on $S \times S$ with marginals $\alpha$ and $\beta$, and $\pi(x,dy)$ a Markov kernel satisfying $Q(dx,dy) =

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T22:11:11.696375+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fb7ce0904ba6cc883fce5c582837e5c506adcefa9c9da36941d7a705dd34d6b5","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:centers of arXiv:2609.00645, 'Global persistence of nearly radial concentrated vortices in a bounded domain'] Let $f\in L^1(\mathbb R^2)$ be nonzero and nonnegative, and set
$\kappa:=\|f\|_1$.  Then $\mathsf C(f)$ is nonempty and compact, and
$\mathcal A(f)<2\kappa$.  Moreover, the following statements hold:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item if $\operatorname{supp}f^*\subset B_r(\mathbf0)$ for some $r>0$,
then every $\mathbf b\in\mathsf C(f)$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
  \int_{\mathbb R^2\setminus B_r(\mathbf b)}f
  \,\mathrm d\mathbf x
  \leq\frac12\mathcal A(f);
\end{equation}
\item if, for some $r,s>0$ and $\mathbf a\in\mathbb R^2$,
\[
  \operatorname{supp}f^*\subset B_r(\mathbf0),
  \qquad
  \operatorname{supp}f\subset B_s(\mathbf a),
\]
then
\begin{equation}
  |\mathbf b-\mathbf a|\leq r+s
  \qquad(\mathbf b\in\mathsf C(f));
\end{equation}
moreover, the mass center $\mathbf X_f$ defined by (equation eq:mass-center of the paper) satisfies
\begin{equation}
  |\mathbf b-\mathbf X_f|
  \leq\frac{r+2s}{\kappa}\mathcal A(f)
  \qquad(\mathbf b\in\mathsf C(f));
\end{equation}
\item if $\operatorname{supp}f^*\subset B_r(\mathbf0)$ for some $r>0$
and $\mathcal A(f)<\kappa$, then
\begin{equation}
  \operatorname{diam}\mathsf C(f)\leq2r;
\end{equation}
\item for any nonzero, nonnegative $f,g\in L^1(\mathbb R^2)$,
\[
  |\mathcal A(f)-\mathcal A(g)|\leq2\|f-g\|_1;
\]
\item the set-valued map $f\mapsto\mathsf C(f)$ has a closed graph with respect
to strong $L^1$ convergence: if $f_n,f\in L^1(\mathbb R^2)$ are nonzero and
nonnegative, then
\[
  f_n\to f\ \text{in }L^1(\mathbb R^2),\qquad
  \mathbf b_n\to\mathbf b\ \text{in }\mathbb R^2,\qquad
  \mathbf b_n\in\mathsf C(f_n)
  \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
  \mathbf b\in\mathsf C(f);
\]
\item the set-valued map $f\mapsto\mathsf C(f)$ is upper semicontinuous\footnote{See
[AubinFrankowska2009] for this standard definition.} with
respect to strong $L^1$ convergence: for every nonzero, nonnegative
$f\in L^1(\mathbb R^2)$ and every open set $O\subset\mathbb R^2$ with
$\mathsf C(f)\subset O$, there exists $\delta>0$ such that
\[
  g\in L^1(\mathbb R^2),\quad g\geq0,\quad g\not\equiv0,\quad
  \|g-f\|_1<\delta
  \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
  \mathsf C(g)\subset O.
\]
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["two-dimensional planar lattice model satisfying the FKG inequality","translation invariance and, in the classical gluing constructions, reflection symmetry of the lattice","an a priori lower bound on square-crossing probabilities, which is a hypothesis to be separately established, not a free consequence of RSW","independence, or at least positive association, of the underlying edge or site variables"],"created_at":"2026-09-07T08:44:20.974286+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fb8fff362c8249e98704b89baabf231efeaf842e818303da3b033c4ea1e6cfba","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). In two-dimensional critical or near-critical percolation, RSW theory states that if crossing probabilities of n x n squares are uniformly bounded away from 0 as n grows, then crossing probabilities of rho n x n rectangles, for any fixed aspect ratio rho, are also uniformly bounded away from 0 (and from 1) by a constant depending on rho but not on n. The classical proof glues together several square-crossing events using the FKG inequality and translation and reflection symmetry of the lattice. RSW estimates are the essential multi-scale input for proving arm-exponent bounds, conformal-invariance-adjacent results, and, via the Duminil-Copin-Tassion approach, for establishing sharpness of the phase transition without relying on exact self-duality. RSW does not by itself prove existence of a scaling limit as n -> infinity, does not give the exact value of any crossing probability, only two-sided bounds; and the classical form required exact self-duality (p=1/2 on the square lattice), so extending the theory to general planar lattices or to p != 1/2 required a genuinely new, duality-free argument (Tassion, 2016). Typical failure: Assuming that RSW-type bounded-away-from-0/1 crossing estimates transfer automatically to a new planar model merely because it is monotone and planar; RSW requires either exact self-duality or the more robust but still nontrivial Tassion-style construction, and models without FKG, or with strong enough long-range dependence, can fail to admit the needed gluing arguments even though they look superficially similar to Bernoulli percolation. Canonical reference: Russo, 1978, Zeitschrift fur Wahrscheinlichkeitstheorie und verwandte Gebiete; Seymour and Welsh, 1978, Annals of Discrete Mathematics; Tassion, 2016, Probability Theory and Related Fields.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["Ω bounded open with Lipschitz boundary, n ≥ 2","1 ≤ p < ∞ for existence, boundedness and kernel; 1 < p < ∞ for the fractional-space range description","Green's identity form: u ∈ H^2(Ω), v ∈ H^1(Ω)"],"created_at":"2026-09-13T01:59:57.492614+00:00","domain":"Sobolev spaces, boundary traces, elliptic boundary value problems","id":"claim_fb9c6a675246add69d2d408b990ef27f4904b933fa93e1e739f05b2304fd2786","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let Ω ⊂ R^n (n ≥ 2) be a bounded open set with Lipschitz boundary, dS the surface measure and ν the outward unit normal (defined dS-a.e.), and let 1 ≤ p < ∞.

(1) Existence and boundedness. There is a unique bounded linear operator T : W^{1,p}(Ω) → L^p(∂Ω, dS) such that Tu = u|_{∂Ω} for every u ∈ W^{1,p}(Ω) ∩ C(Ω̄). Tu is the trace of u, and ||Tu||_{L^p(∂Ω)} ≤ C(Ω, p) ||u||_{W^{1,p}(Ω)}.

(2) Kernel. ker T = W^{1,p}_0(Ω), the closure of C_c^∞(Ω) in W^{1,p}(Ω). A W^{1,p} function vanishes on ∂Ω in the trace sense exactly when it is a W^{1,p}-limit of compactly supported smooth functions.

(3) Range (Gagliardo). For 1 < p < ∞ the range of T is exactly the fractional Sobolev space W^{1−1/p, p}(∂Ω), and T has a bounded linear right inverse W^{1−1/p, p}(∂Ω) → W^{1,p}(Ω). In particular T : H^1(Ω) → H^{1/2}(∂Ω) is bounded and onto, and every g ∈ H^{1/2}(∂Ω) has an extension u ∈ H^1(Ω) with Tu = g and ||u||_{H^1(Ω)} ≤ C ||g||_{H^{1/2}(∂Ω)}. For p = 1 the range is all of L^1(∂Ω). Since H^{1/2}(∂Ω) ↪ L^2(∂Ω) is compact, T : H^1(Ω) → L^2(∂Ω) is a compact operator.

(4) Integration by parts with traces. For u ∈ W^{1,p}(Ω), v ∈ W^{1,p'}(Ω) with 1/p + 1/p' = 1 (p' = ∞ for p = 1) and each i,
   ∫_Ω u ∂_i v dx + ∫_Ω v ∂_i u dx = ∫_∂Ω (Tu)(Tv) ν_i dS.
Hence for u ∈ H^2(Ω), v ∈ H^1(Ω) Green's first identity ∫_Ω ∇u·∇v dx + ∫_Ω (Δu) v dx = ∫_∂Ω (∂_ν u)(Tv) dS holds with ∂_ν u := ν · T(∇u) ∈ L^2(∂Ω), and for u ∈ H^1_0(Ω) all boundary terms vanish.

Where it fails. There is no trace operator on L^p(Ω): ∂Ω has Lebesgue measure zero, an L^p class has no boundary values, and an estimate ||Tu||_{L^p(∂Ω)} ≤ C||u||_{L^p(Ω)} is false (the full W^{1,p} norm is needed). For p > 1 the range is NOT L^p(∂Ω): a general g ∈ L^2(∂Ω) has no H^1(Ω) extension. The kernel and range statements use the Lipschitz boundary (a segment / extension property); for domains with cracks, slits or cusps the boundary is not Lipschitz and these statements need modification (a crack has two sides with two different traces). The trace of ∇u exists for u ∈ H^2(Ω), not for a general u ∈ H^1(Ω), so ∂_ν u is not defined in L^2(∂Ω) for arbitrary H^1 functions.","status":"unverified"}

\[
\mathfrak{v}_{\theta,p}(x)
:=
\theta x^2
-x\log\frac{x}{p}
-(1-x)\log\frac{1-x}{1-p},
\qquad x\in[0,1],

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T13:57:59.861947+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fbd5718058d1f0cb264c841ba513e9a8e94847a5b889598c36ff99354efc8134","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:osi of arXiv:2607.05384, 'Well-invertible column subsets of sparse matrices are rare'] {CamanoEtAl2025}}]

Fix integers $r \le k \le n$ and a parameter $\alpha \in (0,1]$. A random  $n\times k$ matrix $S$
is \emph{$(r,\alpha)$-OSI} if it satisfies the following two conditions:
\begin{itemize}
    \item[(1)] \emph{Isotropy:} for every vector $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$,
    \[
        \mathbb{E} \|S^\top x\|_2^2 = \|x\|_2^2.
    \]
    \item[(2)] \emph{Injectivity:} for every fixed $r$-dimensional subspace $V \subset \mathbb{R}^n$, with probability at least $9/10$,
    \[
        \alpha \|x\|_2^2 \le \|S^\top x\|_2^2
        \qquad \forall x \in V.
    \]
\end{itemize}
The probability $9/10$ in the second condition
can be replaced with another number close to one.","status":"unverified"}
