{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:51:11.954305+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fbda79203ede6d57ec8d3728064ded883d9621c89fa12574c9dcd8f137c061bc","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 17 (Vanishing diagonal regularization) of arXiv:2608.07820, 'Linear Spectral Statistics for Entrywise-Transformed Spiked Wigner Matrices under Shifted '] Let \(\widetilde H\) be a bounded centered array with zero diagonal and an
exactly stochastic, uniformly flat off-diagonal variance matrix
\(\widetilde S\).  Let \(\chi_1,\ldots,\chi_N\) be independent, centered,
variance-one, uniformly bounded random variables, independent of
\(\widetilde H\).  For fixed \(\eta\in(0,1)\), set
\begin{equation}
 \widetilde H^{(\eta)}_{ij}
 :=\sqrt{1-\eta/N}\,\widetilde H_{ij}\quad(i\ne j),
 \qquad
 \widetilde H^{(\eta)}_{ii}:=\sqrt{\eta/N}\,\chi_i.
\end{equation}
Then the variance matrix of \(\widetilde H^{(\eta)}\) is exactly stochastic
and satisfies the uniform lower and upper bounds required by the
generalized-Wigner theorem, with constants allowed to depend on \(\eta\).
For every finite family of functions analytic near \(\Gamma\),
\begin{align}
 \limsup_{N\to\infty}\left|
 \E\Tr\varphi(\widetilde H^{(\eta)})
 -\E\Tr\varphi(\widetilde H)
 \right|&\le C_{\varphi,\Gamma}\eta,
 \\
 \limsup_{N\to\infty}\Var\!\left(
 \Tr\varphi(\widetilde H^{(\eta)})
 -\Tr\varphi(\widetilde H)
 \right)&\le C_{\varphi,\Gamma}\eta.
 
\end{align}
Moreover, the Li--Xu expectation and covariance formulas converge to their flat
zero-diagonal versions in the order \(N\to\infty\), then
\(\eta\downarrow0\).  Consequently the joint CLT for
\(\widetilde H^{(\eta)}\) transfers to \(\widetilde H\).","status":"unverified"}

Using the statistics $S_{00}(A)$ and $S_{rs}(A,U)$ defined in Section 2.4, fix target moments $m_{00}\\in\\mathbb{R}$ and $(m_{rs})_{(r,s)\\in\\mathcal{I}}$ and define $\\mathcal{Q}(m):=\\Bigl\\{Q\\text{ pmf on }\\Omega:\\;\\mathbb{E}_{Q}[S_{00}(A)]=m_{00},\\;\\mathbb{E}_{Q}[S_{rs}(A,U)]=m_{rs}\\ \\ \\forall(r,s)\\in\\mathcal{I}\\Bigr\\}.$ Assume $\\mathcal{Q}(m)\\neq\\varnothing$. (ii) Exponential-family characterisation (attainable moments). For $\\theta=(c,(s_{rs})_{(r,s)\\in\\mathcal{I}})$ define $P_{\\theta}(A\\mid U):=\\exp\\Bigl\\{c\\,S_{00}(A)+\\sum_{(r,s)\\in\\mathcal{I}}s_{rs}S_{rs}(A,U)-\\Psi_{n}(\\theta;U)\\Bigr\\},$ with $\\Psi_{n}(\\theta;U):=\\log\\sum_{A\\in\\Omega}\\exp\\Bigl\\{c\\,S_{00}(A)+\\sum_{(r,s)\\in\\mathcal{I}}s_{rs}S_{rs}(A,U)\\Bigr\\}.$ If there exists $\\theta^{\\star}$ such that $P_{\\theta^{\\star}}(\\cdot\\mid U)\\in\\mathcal{Q}(m)$ (equivalently, $\\mathbb{E}_{\\theta^{\\star}}[S_{00}(A)]=m_{00}$ and $\\mathbb{E}_{\\theta^{\\star}}[S_{rs}(A,U)]=m_{rs}$ for all $(r,s)\\in\\mathcal{I}$), then $Q^{\\star}=P_{\\theta^{\\star}}(\\cdot\\mid U).$ In particular, if one restricts $\\theta$ to the WL–ERG subfamily (e.g. by imposing symmetry constraints inherited from a symmetric coefficient matrix), then any moment-matching WL–ERG member must coincide with $Q^{\\star}$ and hence is the unique maximum–entropy distribution under the constraints. {"assumptions":["driftless subordinator, Levy measure nu = sum_{m>=1} a_m delta_{x_m}","x_m = 4^{-m^2}, a_m = 2^{-m} 4^{m^2}"],"created_at":"2026-09-24T23:46:59.329215+00:00","domain":"probability/Levy processes","id":"claim_fc2810725f4f4b23a924b0d3f7cc75c4","kind":"counterexample","schema_version":1,"statement":"Question 5 of Hu and Sun's survey on Hunt's hypothesis (H) (arXiv:1908.06825) asks whether every pure-jump subordinator with infinite Levy measure satisfies (H). {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T12:33:11.982000+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fc28eb85803580647f89a5389a4a780406a83d14e881b69122aaf6a682d3cc56","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition Interval extension of arXiv:2608.19050, 'Online Permutation Embedding: \\ Optimal Stopping and Scaling Laws'] For the remainder of this section, an \textit{interval} is a closed interval with rational endpoints. An \textit{interval enclosure} of a variable $x$ is an interval $[x] := [\underline{x},\overline{x}] \ni x$. Its width is \(\operatorname{wd}([x])=\overline{x}-\underline{x}\). 
    For a real function $F(x_1,\dots,x_m)$, a function $[F]([x_1],\dots,[x_m])$ is said to be an \textit{interval extension} of $F$ if
    \[
        x_j\in[x_j]\quad (1\le j\le m)
        \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
        F(x_1,\dots,x_m)\in [F]([x_1],\dots,[x_m]).
    \]
    Interval extensions also naturally define operations on intervals. For example,
    \[
    I+J=[\underline I+\underline J,\overline I+\overline J],
    \qquad
    I/c=[\underline I/c,\overline I/c]\quad(c>0).
    \]
    We henceforth implicitly assume all interval operations are performed with ``outward'' rounding (lower endpoints rounded downward and upper endpoints upward) to maintain rationality of the endpoints.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T10:07:48.566545+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fc38cad5596897daed2d2be8002e6feb9e18c80afa03e5ecaecf7e18b92fee3a","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 29 of arXiv:2609.01460, 'On cost-induced Santal\'o-type inequalities \\ in Polish measure spaces'] Let $L\subset M_{n,m}(\R)$ and $K\subset \R^n$ be compact sets of positive volume whose convex hulls contain the (appropriate) origin in their interiors. Then, 
    \[
    \vol[nm](K^{\star,Q})\vol[n](K)^m \leq \vol[nm](K^{\star,Q})\vol[n]((K^{\star,Q})_{\circ,Q})^m 
    \] 
    and 
    \[ 
    \vol[nm](L)\vol[n](L_{\circ,Q})^m \leq \vol[nm]((L_{\circ,Q})^{\star,Q})\vol[n](L_{\circ,Q})^m,
    \]
    with equality only for invariant sets (up to sets of Lebesgue measure zero). 
    
    In particular, the following two statements are equivalent:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item if $K$ or $K^\circ$, has center of mass at the origin, then
    \[
    \vol[nm](K^{\star,Q})\vol[n](K)^m \leq \vol[nm]((\B)^{\star,Q})\vol[n](\B)^m 
    \]
    with equality if and only if $K=E$ for a centered ellipsoid $E\subset\R^n$ up to removal of null sets; 
    \item  if $L_{\circ,Q}$ or $(L_{\circ,Q})^\circ$ has center of mass at the origin, then
    \[
    \vol[nm](L)\vol[n](L_{\circ,Q})^m \leq \vol[nm]((\B)^{\star,Q})\vol[n](\B)^m
    \]
    with equality if and only if $L=E^{\star,Q}$ for a centered ellipsoid $E\subset \R^n$ up to removal of null sets.
    \end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["mu(Omega) < infinity for the global statement; a set of finite measure for the local statement","f_n measurable, f_n -> f mu-almost everywhere, all functions finite a.e."],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:36.752876+00:00","domain":"measure theory","id":"claim_fc6b659554c68f681ea95004be9535b37b79d34316ba22807d81906efef118ad","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Egorov's theorem states that on a FINITE measure space, almost everywhere convergence of measurable functions implies almost uniform convergence: for every eps > 0 there is a measurable E with mu(E) < eps such that the convergence is uniform on the complement of E. Finiteness cannot be dropped. On R with Lebesgue measure let f_n = 1_{[n, n+1]}; then f_n -> 0 at every point, but for ANY set E of finite measure the complement meets [n, n+1] for infinitely many n, so sup over the complement of E of |f_n| equals 1 for infinitely many n and the convergence is not uniform off any set of small measure. What survives on a sigma-finite space is the LOCAL statement: for every measurable A with mu(A) < infinity and every eps > 0 there is E contained in A with mu(E) < eps and uniform convergence on A minus E; equivalently, almost everywhere convergence implies almost uniform convergence on each set of finite measure. The converse implication holds in general: almost uniform convergence always implies convergence almost everywhere and in measure, on any measure space. [standard; e.g. Folland, Real Analysis, 2nd ed., Theorem 2.33 and Exercise 2.39]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T13:54:12.567809+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fc7bc3237410cbf6b684188ecc94f3fab7661bb876adf67616a89e224e9e86d5","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Prop P:half-space-KPZ-horizon-marginals of arXiv:2604.10020, 'The directed landscape in half-space'] As $n\to\infty$, the process $R^{(n)}$ has a distributional limit $R^{\mathsf{KPZ}}=\{R^{\mathsf{KPZ}}_i\}_{i=1}^k$, under the uniform-on-compact topology. 
    We can describe the process $R^{\mathsf{KPZ}}$ explicitly as follows.
	
Let $\mathcal{B} = (\mathcal{B}_1, \mathcal{B}_2, \ldots, \mathcal{B}_{2k})$ be $2k$ independent Brownian motions on $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ of diffusivity $1$, with drift $-\gamma_i$ for $\mathcal{B}_i$ and $\gamma_i$ for $\mathcal{B}_{2k+1-i}$, for each $i\in\llbracket1, k \rrbracket$.
We consider the O'Connell-Yor polymer partition function (see [OYbb]) across $\{\mathcal{B}_i\}_{i=1}^{2k}$, defined as
\[
Z_{\mathcal{B}}(x,i;y,j) = \idotsint_{x=x_i\le \cdots \le x_j \le x_{j+1}=y} \exp\left( \sum_{i'=i}^j \mathcal{B}_{i'}(x_{i'+1})-\mathcal{B}_{i'}(x_{i'}) \right) dx_{i+1}\cdots dx_j,
\]
for any $1\le i \le j \le 2k$, and $0\le x \le y$.

Next, let $\{X(-i, j) : i\in\llbracket1, k \rrbracket, j\in\llbracketi, 2k +1 - i \rrbracket\}$ be an array of inverse gamma random variables, independent of each other and $\mathcal{B}$, satisfying 
\[X(-i, j) \sim \begin{cases}
1 & j =i,\\
\operatorname{Gamma}^{-1}(\gamma_j-\gamma_i), \qquad &j\in\llbracket i + 1, k \rrbracket, \\
\operatorname{Gamma}^{-1}(-\gamma_i- \gamma_{2k + 1 -j}), \qquad &j\in\llbracketk + 1, 2k - i \rrbracket, \\
\operatorname{Gamma}^{-1}(-\gamma_i+\alpha), \qquad &j =  2k + 1- i.
\end{cases}
\]
Then:
\[
R^{\mathsf{KPZ}}_i(x)=
\begin{cases}
\log\left(\frac{\sum_{i\le \ell \le 2k} \big(\sum_{\pi\in P[i,\ell]}\prod_{v\in \pi}X(v)\big)Z_{\mathcal{B}}(0,\ell; x, 2k)}{
\sum_{\pi\in P[i,2k]}\prod_{v\in \pi}X(v) }\right), \qquad & x\ge 0,\\
\log\left(\frac{\sum_{i\le \ell \le 2k} \big(\sum_{\pi\in \hat{P}[i,\ell]}\prod_{v\in \pi}X(v)\big)Z_{\mathcal{B}}(0,\ell; |x|, 2k)}{
\sum_{\pi\in \hat{P}[i,2k]}\prod_{v\in \pi}X(v) }\right), \qquad & x< 0,
\end{cases}
\]
where $P[i,\ell]$ is the collection of all up-right paths in $\mathbb{Z}^2$ from $(-i,i)$ to $(-1,\ell)$, and  
$\hat{P}[i,\ell]$ is the subset of such paths that intersect $\{(x,x+2k+1): x\in \mathbb{Z}\}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-06T03:36:16.740440+00:00","domain":"harvested statement (arXiv 2603.27659, 2026): owner_math","id":"claim_fc8a3d9866d34e7685dd03fa09662144","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 3.11 of arXiv:2603.27659, 'Operator Norm Bounds for Multi-leg Matrix Tensors and Applications to Random Matrix Theory'] Let $m,k,N\\in\\mathbb{N}$, let $\\sigma_{1},\\ldots,\\sigma_{k}\\in\\mathcal{P}^{\\prime}([m])$ be partial permutations, let $A_{1},\\ldots,A_{m}\\in M_{N}(\\mathbb{C})^{\\otimes k}$, let $Y$ be the matrix resulting from the partial trace evaluation $(\\mathrm{Tr}_{\\sigma_{1}}\\otimes\\cdots\\otimes\\mathrm{Tr}_{\\sigma_{k}})(A_{1},\\ldots,A_{m})$, and let $q=\\sum_{j=1}^{k}(m-|D(\\sigma_{j})|)$ with $D(\\sigma_{j})$ the domain of $\\sigma_{j}$, so that $Y$ acts on a space of dimension $N^{q}$. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:16:18.663820+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fc99fa27a2cf04e3db73477c60c3ceca1b51c7646fcf9ee065086a3c193e4d27","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 6 of arXiv:2607.25645, 'Estimates of the total variation distance between laws of Sobolev mappings on Gaussian spa'] Let $k,d\in\mathbb{N}$ with $d\ge 2$, and let $a,b>0$. \[

\bigl(a^{-1}b^{\frac{2k-1}{2}}t\bigr)^\varkappa

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T11:40:59.388433+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fcabd78a1b5baf06f82ad667588fc40d3ca83a9d05fd86df92049096bfee8354","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 4 of arXiv:2609.03968, 'A one-parameter family of local-time conditioned processes : the generalized Brownian burg'] Let $g_0$ be a stretching morphism from some capacity $\lambda$ on an interval $I$ to the constant capacity 1, and fix $x_0\in\overline I$. This means that for $z_0:=g_0(x_0)\in\overline\R$, $g_0$ is a $\mathcal C ^1$-diffeomorphism from $I$ to $\R$ of the form $g_0 : x\in I \mapsto z_0+\int_{x_0}^x {\dd r} / \lambda(r) \in \R $ (understood as a limit when $z_0=\pm\infty$). Let $(D_t)_{0\leq t\leq T}$ be a continuous process with strictly increasing quadratic variation, taking values in $\overline \R = \R\cup\{\pm\infty\}$ (defined up to time-change) and verifying the following two conditions.

\medskip

\noindent
\textnormal{(i) Well-posedness of the flow.}
For every $x\in I$, the integral equation
$$g_t(x)=g_0(x)+\int_0^t\1_{(z_0,g_s(x))}(D_s)\dd[D]_s$$
admits a unique solution until time $T(x):=\inf\{t\geq 0, g_t(x)=\pm\infty\}$, and the map
$(t,x)\mapsto g_t(x)$
is continuous on its domain $\{(t,x), x\in I, 0\le t < T(x)\}$. 

\medskip

\noindent
\textnormal{(ii) Jointly continuous local times along the flow.}
For $x\in I$, assume that the family of processes $(R_t^x)_{0\leq t <T(x)} :=(D_t-g_t(x))_{0\leq t <T(x)} $ admits jointly continuous local
times: namely, assume that there exists a nonnegative field
$(L_t^x(a))_{x\in I,a\in\R,\, 0\leq t<T(x)}$, jointly continuous (at least in a neighborhood of $a=0$)
in $(t,x,a)$, such that for every $x\in I$, every $0\leq t<T(x)$,
and every bounded Borel function $f$,
$$\int_0^t f(R_s^x)\dd[R^x]_s=\int_{\mathbb R}f(a)L_t^x(a)\dd a.
$$

\ms

Write   
$L_t(x):=L_t^x(0).$ For $0\leq t \leq T$, let $I_t := \{ x \in I,\, T(x) > t\}$, and finally let us define for such a process $D$ its final time $T(D) := \inf\{s\leq T,\, \mathring I_s=\emptyset\}\wedge T $.
Then the following properties hold.

\begin{enumerate}
\item For every $0 \leq t < T(D)$, the map $x\mapsto g_t(x)$ is an increasing $C^1$-diffeomorphism from the open interval $I_t := \{ x \in I,\, T(x) > t\}$ to $\R$, with
$$\partial_x g_t(x)=({\exp(L_t(x))}) / {\lambda(x)}.$$

\item  The process $X$ defined for $0\leq t< T(D)$ by
$X_t:=g_t^{-1}(D_t)\in \overline I_t$
is continuous and admits a bicontinuous local time $(\Lambda_t(x))_{0\leq t <T(D),\,x\in I}$, where
$\Lambda_t(x)=\lambda(x)\left(1-\exp\bigl(-L_t(x)\bigr)\right)$, i.e.\ for every bounded Borel function $f$, 
$$\int_0^t f(X_s)\dd[X]_s=\int_{\mathbb R}f(x)\Lambda_t(x)\dd x.
$$
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:02:34.824843+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fcb3169320cd7400e6048b3ca5b434de404a9ce45cab668add20c31fa69ae15f","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 30 (Lyapunov drift for the forward and adjoint chains) of arXiv:2607.19752, 'Weak Equilibrium Measures and Capacity--Hitting Identities\\ for the Hypoelliptic Third-Or'] Assume Assumptions~\ref{ass:U} and~\ref{ass:whole-space-growth}. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T10:42:55.336658+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fcb65a10590ee834330a07c918b367accedcf96958ab8de0266d0ecaefb6f848","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 25 of arXiv:2609.02416, '2609.02416'] The fixed-domain perturbation formulas used later are collected here.

\textup{(i)} Assume the hypotheses of Proposition~\ref{prop:simplicitycore}, so that the principal eigenvalue is simple in the positive cone. Let $h\in C_c(\R)$ satisfy $h\ge0$ and $h\not\equiv0$. Then $\Lp(\cA_\R+h)<\Lp(\cA_\R)$.

\textup{(ii)} Let $b\in C_c(\R)$ satisfy $b\ge0$ and $b\not\equiv0$, and assume that the Lyapunov hypotheses of Proposition~\ref{prop:simplicitycore} hold for every operator $\cA_\R+rb$ under consideration. Then $r\longmapsto\Lp(\cA_\R+rb)$
is strictly decreasing and locally Lipschitz. If there exist $r_-<r_+$ such that the two values have opposite signs, there is a unique $r_*$ with $\Lp(\cA_\R+r_*b)=0$.

\textup{(iii)} Let $\Omega=(\alpha,\beta)$ be fixed. Let
\[
\cA_\tau u=d\int_\Omega\big(J(x-y)+\tau H(x,y)\big)u(y)\,dy+\big(q(x)+\tau r(x)\big)u'(x)+\big(b(x)+\tau h(x)\big)u(x),
\]
where $q,r\in C^1(\overline \Omega)$, $b,h\in C(\overline \Omega)$ and $H\in C(\overline \Omega^2)$.  We restrict $\tau$ to a real interval on which the drift is bounded away from zero and the kernels $J(x-y)+\tau H(x,y)$ are nonnegative and satisfy a common positivity condition in a neighborhood of the diagonal. Let $\lambda(\tau)=\Lp(\cA_\tau)$. Then the principal eigenvalue and the normalized principal eigenfunction are real analytic in $\tau$ on that interval. If $\phi,\phi^*>0$ are the direct and adjoint principal eigenfunctions at $\tau=0$, normalized by $\int_\Omega\phi\phi^*\,dx=1$,
then
\[
\begin{aligned}
\lambda'(0)={}&-d\int_\Omega\int_\Omega\phi^*(x)H(x,y)\phi(y)\,dy\,dx\\
&-\int_\Omega r(x)\phi'(x)\phi^*(x)\,dx
-\int_\Omega h(x)\phi(x)\phi^*(x)\,dx.
\end{aligned}
\]
In particular, for a potential perturbation alone,
\[
\lambda'(0)=-\int_\Omega h(x)\phi(x)\phi^*(x)\,dx.
\]

\textup{(iv)} On a fixed bounded interval let
\[
\cA_{d,c}u=d\left(\int_\Omega J(x-y)u(y)\,dy-u(x)\right)+c\,r(x)u'(x)+a(x)u(x),
\]
where $d>0$, $c$ ranges in an interval on which $cr(x)$ has a fixed sign bounded away from zero, and $r\in C^1(\overline \Omega)$. Normalize the direct and adjoint eigenfunctions by $\int_\Omega\phi\phi^*=1$. Then the principal eigenvalue and the normalized eigenfunction are real analytic in $(d,c)$ on every connected parameter region on which $d>0$ and $cr$ keeps a fixed sign bounded away from zero, and
\[
\partial_d\Lp=-\int_\Omega\phi^*(x)\left(\int_\Omega J(x-y)\phi(y)\,dy-\phi(x)\right)dx,
\]
\[
\partial_c\Lp=-\int_\Omega r(x)\phi'(x)\phi^*(x)\,dx.
\]
No sign is asserted for these derivatives in general.

\textup{(v)} For the scaled operator
\[
\cA_{\sigma,m,L}u=\frac1{\sigma^m}\left(\int_{-L}^{L}J_\sigma(x-y)u(y)\,dy-u(x)\right)+q(x)u'(x)+a(x)u(x),
\]
put $\rho=\sigma/L$ and $v(\xi)=u(L\xi)$. Then
\[
\Lp(\cA_{\sigma,m,L})=\Lp\left(L^{-m}\rho^{-m}(\mathcal J_\rho-I)+L^{-1}q(L\cdot)\partial_\xi+a(L\cdot),(-1,1)\right),
\]
where
\[
\mathcal J_\rho v(\xi)=\int_{-1}^{1}J_\rho(\xi-\eta)v(\eta)\,d\eta.
\]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["γ is a closed piecewise C^1 curve (or a cycle) in C","the point a does not lie on the trace of γ"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:49:42.483563+00:00","domain":"complex analysis","id":"claim_fcf7242c6dd1f3172a2cc112bfa1af26bdbbd80032c909e06e994d0138efa1ef","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let γ : [α,β] → C be a closed piecewise C^1 curve and let a be a point not on the trace of γ. The winding number (index) of γ about a is n(γ,a) = (1/2πi) ∫_γ dz/(z - a). It is always an integer; as a function of a it is constant on each connected component of the complement of the trace of γ, and it is 0 on the unbounded component. The definition extends additively to cycles (finite formal integer combinations of closed curves) and, via continuous branches of the argument, to merely continuous closed curves. A cycle γ lying in an open set U is called null-homologous in U (homologous to zero) if n(γ,w) = 0 for every w in C minus U. An open connected U ⊂ C is simply connected if and only if every cycle in U is null-homologous in U, if and only if the complement of U in the Riemann sphere is connected. The homology form of Cauchy's theorem reads: if f is holomorphic on U and γ is a cycle null-homologous in U, then ∫_γ f(z) dz = 0 and n(γ,z) f(z) = (1/2πi) ∫_γ f(ζ)/(ζ - z) dζ for every z in U off the trace of γ.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-08-02T18:00:45.293750+00:00","domain":"QA-corrected (round 3, audit-driven)","id":"claim_fd20eb546203a01373d765977397366face1474bc7d2f53f769a6549383d7382","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Seifert-Van Kampen theorem: Let X be a topological space written as X = U union V, where U and V are open and path-connected and the intersection U intersect V is nonempty and path-connected, and choose a basepoint x_0 in U intersect V. Let i and j denote the homomorphisms pi_1(U intersect V, x_0) -> pi_1(U, x_0) and pi_1(U intersect V, x_0) -> pi_1(V, x_0) induced by inclusion. Then pi_1(X, x_0) is the pushout of i and j, i.e. the free product with amalgamation pi_1(U, x_0) * pi_1(V, x_0) modulo the normal subgroup generated by all elements i(g) j(g)^{-1} with g in pi_1(U intersect V, x_0). In particular, if U intersect V is simply connected then pi_1(X, x_0) is the free product pi_1(U, x_0) * pi_1(V, x_0). This lets one compute fundamental groups of spaces built from simpler pieces.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["k algebraically closed (over R, for example, x^2 + 1 has no zero and the weak form fails)"],"created_at":"2026-08-29T02:26:24.138161+00:00","domain":"commutative algebra / algebraic geometry","id":"claim_fd299ef0d812bc84f4e522b64f80b42912c4b2149be4e4eed7dcbbb09198fcc4","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let k be an algebraically closed field and R = k[x_1, ..., x_n]. Weak form: every proper ideal I of R has a common zero, that is, V(I) = {a in k^n : f(a) = 0 for all f in I} is nonempty; equivalently every maximal ideal of R has the form (x_1 - a_1, ..., x_n - a_n). {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-28T00:48:45.312498+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fd3771e65f917fea5d179b280898c754cbb7c13e975ed28cafdad6ec9c7e3c95","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:cone of arXiv:2411.14921, 'A boundary Harnack principle and its application to analyticity of 3D Brownian intersectio'] For any $u_1>1$, we choose a small constant $d_0>0$ and a large constant $n_1>64\, d_0^2$ such that the following construction is possible for all $n>n_1$ and $1\le m\le n$. 
    \begin{enumerate}[label=$\bullet$]
        \item On the unit sphere, we pick $n$ unit vectors $(v_i)_{1\le i\le n}$ such that $|v_i-v_{i'}|>12\,d_0\,n^{-1/2}$ for any $1\le i<i'\le n$. Let $S_i:=\mathsf{C}(v_i,d_0/\sqrt n)$, $1\le i\le n$, be $n$ disjoint cones.
        \item On each surface $S_i\cap\partial \mathcal{B}_0$, we further pick $m$ points $v_{i,j}$ along an arc such that the following properties hold.
        Let $c_0$ and $c_1$ be two small positive constants. Consider two smaller cones
        \[
        T_{i,j}:=\mathsf{C}(v_{i,j},u_1^{-n}) \quad \text{and} \quad V_{i,j}:=\mathsf{C}(v_{i,j},c_0m^{-1}n^{-1/2}).
        \]
        For any $i,j$, we have $T_{i,j}\subseteq V_{i,j}\subseteq S_i$, $\mathrm{dist}(v_{i,j},\partial S_i)\ge c_1\, n^{-1/2}$, and $V_{i,j}\cap V_{i,l}=\varnothing$ if $j\neq l$. Moreover, if $1\le j<l\le m$, then $ |z/|z|-v_{i,l}|\geq c_1|j-l|/(m\sqrt n)$  for every $z\in V_{i,j}$.
    \end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

		Let $T > 0$, and let $\{X^n\}$ be a sequence of c\`adl\`ag $\Rd$-valued processes on $[0,T]$.
		If the following two conditions hold, then $\{X^n\}$ is tight in $D([0,T]; \Rd)$:
		\begin{enumerate}
			\item For every $t \in [0,T]$, the family of laws of $\{X^n_t\}$ is tight in $\Rd$.
			\item For every $\eta > 0$ and every sequence of stopping times $\{\tau_n\}$ bounded by $T$,
			\[
			\lim_{\delta \to 0} \limsup_{n \to \infty} \sup_{0 \le \theta \le \delta} \P\left( |X^n_{(\tau_n + \theta) \wedge T} - X^n_{\tau_n}| \ge \eta \right) = 0\,.
			\]
		\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:48:27.280242+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fd54e787f160cbd54f330787b493bf255766b598fb650fb4c0a42ccdd0f8f3c4","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 26 of arXiv:2604.24684, 'Waning Immunity Fails to Restore a Positive Epidemic Threshold on Power--Law Networks'] Fix any $\delta\in(0,1)$, and set
$
\tilde{\varepsilon}:=\frac{\delta}{20\tau},
\bar\varepsilon:=\frac{\tilde{\varepsilon}}{4.4\tau},
\varepsilon:=\frac{\bar\varepsilon}{4\tau}
$.
Let $G=G(n,\tau)$ be a power-law random graph on $n$ vertices with exponent $\tau>2$, and let
$
\bm d=(d_1,\dots,d_n)
$
denote its degree sequence. Suppose that $v_1,\dots,v_{\lceil n^{1-\delta}\rceil}$ are vertices with degrees greater than $n^{2\tilde\varepsilon}$. Let $\tilde A$ denote the event that, for each $a=1,\dots,\lceil n^{1-\delta}\rceil$, the vertex $v_a$ has at least $\lceil n^{\tilde\varepsilon}\rceil$ pairwise distinct neighbors
$
u_1^{(a)},\dots,u_{\lceil n^{\tilde\varepsilon}\rceil}^{(a)}
$
such that all vertices in the collection
$
\{u_b^{(a)}:1\le a\le \lceil n^{1-\delta}\rceil ,\ 1\le b\le \lceil n^{\tilde\varepsilon}\rceil\}
$
are distinct, and have degrees between $n^{\bar\varepsilon}$ and $n^{3\bar\varepsilon}
$. Moreover, for each $a=1,\dots,\lceil n^{1-\delta}\rceil$ and each $b=1,\dots, \lceil n^{\tilde\varepsilon}\rceil$, the vertex $u_b^{(a)}$ has at least $ \lceil n^{\varepsilon}\rceil$ distinct neighbors
$
w_{a,b,1},\dots,w_{a,b,\lceil n^{\varepsilon}\rceil}
$
such that all vertices in the collection
$
\{w_{a,b,m}:1\le a\le\lceil n^{1-\delta}\rceil,\ 1\le b\le \lceil n^{\tilde\varepsilon}\rceil,\ 1\le m\le\lceil n^{\varepsilon}\rceil\}
$
are distinct and have degrees between
$n^{\varepsilon}$ and $n^{3\varepsilon}$. Then, for all sufficiently large $n$,
\begin{equation}
\mathbb P(\tilde A\mid \bm d)\ge 1-\exp(-n^{\bar\varepsilon(\tau-2)/2})-\exp(-n^{\varepsilon/2}), \qquad \text{on the event $D_{\varepsilon}$ defined in \eqref{eq_D}. }
\end{equation}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:38:13.643698+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fd6ff510501e8fffde2302a15f6c21d928dfdae69dd1ad6e5729b2866bd95456","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 3 (Viscosity solutions of the obstacle problem) of arXiv:2609.00703, 'Ellipsoidal Positivity Sets for Fractional Obstacle Problems with Quadratic Forcing'] Let \(f\in C(\mathbb R^n)\).

A function \(u\in C_b(\mathbb R^n)\) is a viscosity subsolution of \eqref{eq:obstacle}
if, whenever \(x_0\in\mathbb R^n\), \(r>0\), and
\(\phi\in C^2(B_r(x_0))\cap C(\overline{B_r(x_0)})\) are such that
\[
u(x_0)=\phi(x_0),
\qquad
u\le\phi
\quad\text{in }B_r(x_0),
\]
one has \(u(x_0)\le0\) or
\[
\mathcal L_r[\phi,u](x_0)-f(x_0)\le0.
\]

A function \(u\in C_b(\mathbb R^n)\) is a viscosity supersolution of \eqref{eq:obstacle}
if \(u\ge0\) in \(\mathbb R^n\) and, whenever \(x_0\in\mathbb R^n\), \(r>0\), and
\(\phi\in C^2(B_r(x_0))\cap C(\overline{B_r(x_0)})\) are such that
\[
u(x_0)=\phi(x_0),
\qquad
u\ge\phi
\quad\text{in }B_r(x_0),
\]
one has
\[
\mathcal L_r[\phi,u](x_0)-f(x_0)\ge0.
\]

A function \(u\in C_b(\mathbb R^n)\) is a viscosity solution of \eqref{eq:obstacle}
if it is both a viscosity subsolution and a viscosity supersolution.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-28T02:56:14.237827+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fda39fb63d5bb25b7c8a8bff90c5e20b44a62f742cbaa054b6cfe8a8bb83ae5d","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma generalMDP of arXiv:2412.09471, 'On the moderate deviation principles in the sparse multi-type Erd\H{o}s R\'enyi random gra'] Let $a_n$ be a sequence such that $1\ll a_n\ll\sqrt{n}$.   $${\mathbb E} \xi^{n,1}=m+O(\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}),$$
  and $${\mathbb E}(\xi^{n,1}_i-m_i)(\xi^{n,1}_j-m_j)=\sigma_{ij}+O(\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}),$$
  for some $m\in{\mathbb R}^d$ and some covariance matrix $C=(\sigma_{ij})_{d\times d}$. Let $b_n\in{\mathbb R}^d$ be a sequence such that $|b_{n}|=O\left(\sqrt{n}+a_n^2\right)$.
  Suppose that there exists $R>0$ such that for all $\eta\in{\mathbb R}^d$ and $|\eta|<R$, $\sup_n\log {\mathbb E}\exp(\eta\cdot \xi^n)<\infty$. 
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
    \item   Let $N(\lambda_n n)$ be an independent Poisson process with $\lambda_n=\lambda+O(\frac{1}{n})$. The sequence of random variables 
    $$\frac{\sum_{k=1}^{N(\lambda_n n)}\xi^{n,k}-\lambda m n+b_n}{a_n\sqrt{n}}$$
    satisfies the moderate deviation principle in ${\mathbb R}^d$ with speed $a_n^2$ and the rate function 
    \[
    \sup_{l\in{\mathbb R}^d}\left\{\langle l,x\rangle-\frac\lambda{2}\langle l, (C+mm^T)l\rangle\right\}.
    \]
    Moreover, when the matrix $C+mm^T$ is positive-definite, the rate function equals  
    $${\frac{1}{2\lambda}\<x,(C+mm^T)^{-1}x\>.}$$
    \item For any $\lambda>0$ and $u\in{\mathbb R}$, the sequence of random variables 
    $$\frac{\sum_{k=1}^{\lfloor\lambda n+ua_n\sqrt{n}\rfloor}\xi^{n,k}-(\lambda n+ua_n\sqrt{n})m+b_n}{a_n\sqrt{n}}$$
    satisfies the moderate deviation principle in ${\mathbb R}^d$ with speed $a_n^2$ and the rate function
    \[
    \sup_{l\in{\mathbb R}^d}\left\{\langle l,x\rangle-\frac\lambda{2}\langle l, C l\rangle\right\}.
    \]
    Moreover, when the matrix $C$ is positive-definite, the rate function equals
    $${\frac{1}{2\lambda}\<x,C^{-1}x\>.}$$
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:59:53.160538+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fdafdc6845ce4f5b20d1c730af2ada58b496c5e19f2e811ff6e9dea9ab4d33c4","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 12 of arXiv:2607.02434, 'A Topological Formula for \\ Potts Lattice Gauge Theory Correlations'] The $i$-dimensional \textbf{plaquette random cluster model (PRCM)} with free boundary conditions on a finite cell complex $X$ with parameters $p\in\brac{0,1}$ and $q\in\N_{\geq 2}$ is the random $i$-complex $P$ with the following distribution:
$$\mu^{\mathbf{f}}_{X}\paren{P} = \mu^{\mathbf{f}}_{X,p,q}\paren{P} \propto p^{\abs{P}}\paren{1-p}^{\abs{X^{i}} - \abs{P}}\abs{H^{i-1}\paren{P;\Z_q}}$$
where $\abs{X^{\paren{i}}}$ and $\abs{P}$ denote the number of $i$-faces $X$ and $P.$

Moreover, if $\Lambda=\brac{-N,N}^d\subset \Z^d$ is a box, the PRCM with wired boundary conditions on $\Lambda$ is the measure
$$\mu^{\mathbf{w}}_{\Lambda}\paren{P} = \mu^{\mathbf{w}}_{\Lambda,p,q}\paren{P} \propto p^{\abs{P}}\paren{1-p}^{\abs{\Lambda^{\paren{i}}} - \abs{P}}\abs{H^{i-1}\paren{P\cup \partial \Lambda;\Z_q}}\,.$$
The weak limits of these measures as $\Lambda\nearrow \Z^d$ exist by standard stochastic monotonicity arguments and are denoted by $\mu^{\mathbf{f}}_{\Z^d,p,q}$ and $\mu^{\mathbf{w}}_{\Z^d,p,q}.$","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:25:44.985763+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fde6c6e50b8c4feef9dccacd692b24154833dae8fa80999538fb7083d334bf4e","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Thm 5 (Stability of compensated jump functionals under quadratic variation convergence) of arXiv:2605.11783, 'Stability of Compensated Jump Integrals under Quadratic Variation Convergence'] Let \(X\) and \(\{X^n\}_{n\ge 1}\) be real-valued càdlàg processes on
\([0,t]\), with jump measures \(\mu\) and \(\mu^n\), and predictable
compensators \(\nu\) and \(\nu^n\), respectively. Assume that 
\[
        [X^n-X]_t \longrightarrow 0
        \quad\text{in probability.}
\]

Let \(f\) and \(f_n\), \(n\ge 1\), be predictable functions on
\(\Omega\times[0,t]\times\mathbb R\), 
such that the compensated jump integrals
\[
        M_t
        :=
        \int_0^t\int_{\mathbb R}
        f(s,x,\omega)(\mu-\nu)(ds,dx),
\]
and
\[
        M^n_t
        :=
        \int_0^t\int_{\mathbb R}
        f_n(s,x,\omega)(\mu^n-\nu^n)(ds,dx)
\]
are well-defined purely discontinuous local martingales.
Assume that $\P\left(\exists s\le t: \Delta X_s(\omega)\in \mathrm{disc}(f(s,.,\omega))\right)=0$.
Assume moreover that, for every \(a>0\), there exists a nonnegative
predictable process \(C^a\), locally bounded on \([0,t]\), such that, for
all \(n\ge1\),
\[
|f_n(s,x,\omega)|+|f(s,x,\omega)|
\le C^a_s(\omega)|x|,
\qquad s\le t,\ |x|\le a .
\]
Assume also that there exists a set \(\Omega_0\in\mathcal F\) with
\(\mathbb P(\Omega_0)=1\) such that, for every \(\omega\in\Omega_0\), every
\(s\leq t\), and every compact set \(K\subset\mathbb R\),
\[
        \sup_{x\in K}|f_n(s,x,\omega)-f(s,x,\omega)|\longrightarrow 0 .
\]

Then
\[
        M^n \longrightarrow M
        \quad\text{ucp on }[0,t].
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:46:26.254038+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fdf02d2b6104afbdbcf90130e4177d3eaf0c663b09f7dc5685c6ae02f04f3e8d","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Prp 11 of arXiv:2605.23308, 'Convergence rate estimates for semigroups and heat kernels associated with resistance form'] For a boundedly compact metric space $(X,d^X)$ and $\rho_X\in X$, we have the following.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-28T02:39:12.419501+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fdf17a2196d1cd144b6bea42b0864612ee5dc28726429d62afb8ae8373930a0d","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Dfn 3. dfn: functor of arXiv:2412.08236, 'Aging and sub-aging for Bouchaud trap models on resistance metric spaces'] [{Functor}] 
  We call $\tau$ a \textit{functor} on $\mathfrak{M}_{c}$ if it satisfies the following.
  \begin{enumerate} [label = (\roman*)]
    \item 
      For every $ (S, d^{S}, \rho_{S}) \in \mathfrak{M}_{c}$,
      one has a metric space $(\tau(S, d^{S}, \rho_{S}), d_{\tau}^{S, \rho_{S}})$
      where $\tau(S, d^{S}, \rho_{S})$ is a set and $d_{\tau}^{S, \rho_{S}}$ is a metric on it.
      We simply write $\tau(S) \coloneqq \tau(S, d^{S}, \rho_{S})$.
    \item 
      For every $(S_{i}, d^{S_{i}}, \rho_{S_{i}}),\, i=1,2$ 
      and root-and-distance-preserving map $f: S_{1} \to S_{2}$, 
      one has a distance-preserving map $\tau_{f}: \tau(S_{1}) \to \tau(S_{2})$.
    \item 
      For any two root-and-distance-preserving maps $f :S_{1} \to S_{2},\, g : S_{2} \to S_{3}$,
      it holds that $\tau_{g \circ f} = \tau_{g} \circ \tau_{f}$.
    \item 
      For any $(S, d^{S}, \rho_{S}) \in \mathfrak{M}_{c}$, 
      it holds that $\tau_{\id_{S}} = \id_{\tau(S)}$.
  \end{enumerate}
  Similarly, we call $\tau$ a functor on $\mathfrak{M}$ if it satisfies the same conditions 
  not for $\mathfrak{M}_{c}$ but for $\mathfrak{M}$.","status":"unverified"}

Then, for every pair of mappings $f=(f_1,\ldots,f_k)$ and $g=(g_1,\ldots,g_k)$ with
$f_j,g_j\in W^{2,p}(\gamma)$,
\[
\max_{1\le j\le k}\|f_j\|_{\dot W^{2,p}(\gamma)}\le b,
\quad
\max_{1\le j\le k}\|g_j\|_{\dot W^{2,p}(\gamma)}\le b,
\]
and
\[
\gamma(\Delta_f\le \varepsilon)\le a\varepsilon^\varkappa,
\quad
\gamma(\Delta_g\le \varepsilon)\le a\varepsilon^\varkappa
\quad \forall\, \varepsilon>0,
\]
one has
\[
d_{\mathrm{TV}}(f,g)
\le
2^{14}k^{7/2}(q-\varkappa)^{-1}(a+b^p+1)\,
d_{\mathrm{KR}}(f,g)^{\beta_1}.
\]
More generally, for every $r\in\mathbb{N}$,
\[
d_{\mathrm{TV}}(f,g)
\le
C(r,k)(q-\varkappa)^{-1}(a+b^p+1)\,
d_r(f,g)^{\beta_r},

where

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T10:25:49.846925+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fe1c10e6a2d337214951b6efe897be373e6635ae64603bdae0fc5d41175318bb","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 10 of arXiv:2609.01996, 'Baumslag--Solitar Subgroups Obstruct Model Companions for Fields with Group Actions'] Let \(H\leq G\), let \(K\) be a \(G\)-field, and let \(\chi:H\to K^\times\) satisfy the \(1\)-cocycle condition

  \[

  \]
  and put
  \[
    \alpha(\gamma,\lambda):=\rho(\gamma\lambda)^{-1}\gamma\rho(\lambda)\quad(\gamma\in G,\ \lambda\in G/H).
  \]
  If the elements \(z_\lambda\), \(\lambda\in G/H\), are algebraically independent over \(K\), then the formulas

  extend the given action on \(K\) to a \(G\)-field structure on the purely transcendental extension
  \[

        &\WERR(\cA_{N_j}, \mu)
        =\max\bigg\{
            \bbW_2\Big( \mu(\cA_{N_j}), \mu \Big),
            \bbW_2\Big(\mu^{\Ising}(\cA_{N_j}), \cP(\{\pm 1\}) \Big)
        \bigg\} \le \epsilon\,, \\
        &q_0(j) \equiv \chi_{\cA_{N_j}}(0) 
        = \frac{\|\bbE \bsig_j\|_2^2}{N_j} 
        \stackrel{j\to\infty}{\longrightarrow} 1
        \,,
    \end{align*}
where we abbreviate $\bsig_j\equiv \cA_{N_j}(\bG,\bg^\aux)$. 
    Define the perturbed (deterministic) algorithm $\tilde\cA_{N_j}$ by setting 
    \[
        \tilde{\bsig}_j
        \equiv \tilde\cA_{N_j}(\bG,\bg^\aux) 
        = \frac{\bbE\bsig_j}{q_0(j)^{1/2}} \,.
    \]
This clearly satisfies $\bbE[\|\tilde{\bsig}_j\|_2^2]  = N_j$, so $\tilde\cA_{N_j}$ is a $0$-Lipschitz algorithm in the sense of Definition~\ref{d:Lip}.
Since $\tilde{\bsig}_j$ is a deterministic vector in $N_j$ dimensions of norm $(N_j)^{1/2}$, we have $\mu(\tilde \cA_{N_j}) = \cN(0,1)$.
    Note that
    \begin{align*}
        \frac{\bbE[
            \|\bsig_j - \tilde{\bsig}_j\|^2]}{N_j} 
        &= \frac{1}{N_j} \bbE\bigg[ \bigg\|
            \bigg(\frac{1}{q_0(j)^{1/2}} - 1 \bigg) 
            	(\bbE\bsig_j)
            - (\bsig_j - \bbE\bsig_j)
        \bigg\|^2 \bigg] \\
        &= \Big(1 - q_0(j)^{1/2}\Big)^2 + \Big(1 - q_0(j)\Big)
        \le 2\Big(1-q_0(j)\Big)\,,
    \end{align*}  
again using that inequality $|x^{1/2}-y^{1/2}| \le |x-y|^{1/2}$ for $x,y\ge0$.
    Then, by Lemma~\ref{l:control.problems.approx}, with constants $c_0$, $C_1(\alpha)$, $C_2(\alpha,L)$ as defined therein, we have
    \[
        \bbW_2\Big(\mu(\cA_{N_j}),
        	\mu(\tilde \cA_{N_j}) = \cN(0,1) 
	\Big)
        \le \bigg\{
        C_1(\alpha) 2(1-q_0(j)) + C_2(\alpha,L) e^{-c_0N_j} \bigg\}^{1/2}\,.
    \]
Combined with the assumption that $\bbW_2(\mu(\cA_{N_j}), \mu) \le \epsilon$ for all $j$, we find $\bbW_2(\mu,\cN(0,1)) \le \epsilon$.
    Since this holds for all $\epsilon > 0$, we conclude $\mu = \cN(0,1)$.
    We have thus shown $\sM^{\Lip}(\alpha,1) \subseteq \{\cN(0,1)\}$.
    The reverse inclusion $\cN(0,1) \in \sM^{\Lip}(\alpha,1)$ is witnessed by the (sequence of) deterministic algorithms
    \[
        \cA_N(\bG,\bg^{\aux}) = (1,\ldots,1) \in \bbR^N\,, 
    \]
    which are $0$-Lipschitz with $\mu(\cA_N) = \cN(0,1)$, $\mu^{\Ising}(\cA_N) = \delta_1 \in \cP(\{\pm 1\})$, and $\chi_{\cA_N}(0) = 1$.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:09:43.712563+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_feaba3cd7651eeae98cfef872e7da6be688c330e8fd8c20a8243d425094ea1e9","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition t.randomfieldCLT-new of arXiv:2605.28430, 'Limit theory for Lipschitz-localized statistics in random geometric models'] Let $M=\{M(x)\}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^d}$ be a random field in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with values in a Polish space
$\mathbb {M} $ and $\zeta: \mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb {M}  \to \mathbb{R}$ a  measurable function. 
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a simple point process on $\mathbb{R}^d $,
independent of the random field $M$. 
Consider empirical random measures $(\hat{\sigma}_{n}^{\zeta(M)})_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ as in (equation linearstatBsigma of the paper).
\begin{enumerate}[wide,label=(\roman*),labelindent=0pt]
\item 
Assume that $\mathcal{P}$ has fast mixing correlations 
as in Definition~(d.omegamixing of the paper)(i.mixing-ground-fast of the paper). Assume that either (a) the random field $M$ satisfies the fast $\mathbb{B} $-mixing condition of Definition~(d.omegatmixing-field of the paper)(i.B-mixing-field of the paper)-(i.mixing-field-fast of the paper) or (b) 
$M$  satisfies the fast \textnormal{BL}-mixing condition of Definition~(d.omegatmixing-field of the paper)(i.BL-mixing-field of the paper)-(i.mixing-field-fast of the paper)
and $\zeta(x,\cdot)$ is Lipschitz. If $\zeta$ satisfies the $p$-moment condition~(equation e:M-p-moment of the paper) with respect to $M$ for all $p>1$ then the central limit theorem holds for
    $(\hat\sigma_{n}^{\zeta(M)}(f))_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$, i.e., as $n \to \infty$

\[   ({\rm Var} \, \hat\sigma_{n}^{\zeta(M)}(f) )^{-1/2}\Big( \hat\sigma_{n}^{\zeta(M)}(f) - \mathbb {E}  \hat\sigma_{n}^{\zeta(M)}(f) \Big) \stackrel{d}{\Rightarrow} Z,
  \]
for $f \in \mathbb{B} (W_1)$,  provided
${\rm Var} \, {\hat{\sigma}_{n}^{\zeta(M)}(f)} = \Omega(n^{\nu})$ for some $\nu > 0$.

\item  
Suppose the random field~$M$ and the point process~$\mathcal{P}$ are stationary 
(necessarily jointly so, due to their independence) with~$\mathcal{P}$ having intensity~$\rho$, 
and suppose that~$\zeta$ is translation invariant, 
i.e., $\zeta(x,\cdot) = \zeta(\cdot)$. Also assume $\zeta$ satisfies the $(1+\epsilon)$-moment condition~(equation e:M-p-moment of the paper) with respect to $M$ for some $\epsilon > 0$.
Then the mean empirical field satisfies for all $f \in \mathbb{B} (W_1)$
\begin{equation}
n^{-1} \, \mathbb{E}  \, \hat\sigma_n^{\zeta(M)}(f)
= \rho\, \mathbb {E}  \, \zeta(\0,M(\0)) \int_{W_1} f(x)\, \mathrm{d} x, \quad n\in\mathbb{N},
\end{equation}
which holds  without assuming mixing conditions on~$\mathcal{P}$ and~$M$ nor  Lipschitz conditions on $\zeta$. Moreover, under either of the mixing assumptions (a) or (b) of part~(i.CLT-infinite-zeta-field-mixing of the paper) we obtain for all $f \in \mathbb{B} (W_1)$
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty} n^{-1} {\rm Var} \, \hat\sigma_{n}^{\zeta(M)}(f)
= \sigma^2(\zeta) \int_{W_1} f(x)^2\,\mathrm{d} x,
\]
where
\begin{align}  
\sigma^2(\zeta) 
&:= \rho\, \mathbb {E}  \, \zeta^2(\0,M(\0)) \\
&\quad + \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} 
\Big( 
\mathbb {E} [\zeta(\0,M(\0))\, \zeta(x,M(x))]\, \rho^{(2)}(\0,x)
- \rho^2\, \mathbb {E} [\zeta(\0,M(\0))]\, \mathbb {E} [\zeta(x,M(x))]  
\Big)\, \mathrm{d} x \in [0, \infty) \nonumber
\end{align}
provided that~$\zeta$ satisfies the $(2+\epsilon)$-moment condition~(equation e:M-p-moment of the paper) for some $\epsilon > 0$.
\item  Let

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:33:12.357430+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_feb7ff89f7ecb021ab1aa195f46a8f119ae55386714824dd65634a1101bfea88","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem 241 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For any $\alpha,\iota > 0$ and $\fq\in [1,2)$ there exists $\epsilon = \epsilon(\alpha,\iota,\fq) > 0$ such that 
	\[
	\max\bigg\{
	\bbW_\fq(\mu,\ocM^{\Ising}(\alpha)) 
	: \mu\in \cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;\epsilon)
	\bigg\}
	\le \iota\,.
	\]
The same statement holds with
$\ocM^{\Ising,\sym}(\alpha)$ and
$\cM^{\Lip,\sym}(\alpha;\epsilon)$ in place of $\ocM^{\Ising}(\alpha)$
and $\cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;\epsilon)$. (The sets mentioned above specified by Definition~\ref{d:achievable-msrs}, \eqref{e:cM.Lip.union.L}, and \eqref{e:cM.Lip.union.L.SYM}.)

\begin{proof} Let
$\cA_N$ be an $L$-Lipschitz algorithm. 
If $\mu \in \cP_2(\R)$ satisfies $\bbW_2(\mu(\cA_N),\mu) \le \epsilon$, then Lemma~\ref{l:lip.alg.l2.l4.bound} gives, for $N$ large enough,
	\[
	\|\mu\|_{L^2} 
	\le 
	\|\mu(\cA_N)\|_{L^2} 
	+ \bbW_2(\mu(\cA_N),\mu)
	\stackrel{\eqref{e:lip.alg.l2.l4.bound.l2}}{\le} 
	C(\alpha)^{1/2} + \epsilon
	\le (2C(\alpha))^{1/2}\,,
	\]
where the last bound holds for $\epsilon$ small enough. For such $\epsilon$, it follows by recalling \eqref{e:cM.Lip.union.L} and \eqref{e:cM.Lip} that 
	\[\cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;\epsilon) 
	\stackrel{\eqref{e:cM.Lip.union.L}}{=}
	\bigcup_{L>0}
		\cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;L,\epsilon) \subseteq \cP_2(\R,2C(\alpha))\,.
	\]
For $\iota > 0$, define the set
	\[
		S_\iota = \Big\{\mu \in \cP_2(\R,2C(\alpha)) : \bbW_\fq(\mu,\ocM^{\Ising}(\alpha)) \ge \iota\Big\}\,.
	\]
	Now suppose for contradiction that $\cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;\epsilon)$ intersects $S_\iota$ for all $\epsilon > 0$.
	Recall from Lemma~\ref{l:confinement.cPp.compact.Wq} that the $\cP_2(\R,2C(\alpha))$
	endowed with the $\bbW_\fq$ metric
	 is compact.
	The set $S_\iota$ is closed with respect to this metric. Thus, for any sufficiently small $\epsilon > 0$, the set
	\[
		S_\iota \cap \overline{\cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;\epsilon)}
	\]
	(where the overline now denotes closure with respect to the $\bbW_\fq$ metric) is a nonempty closed subset of $\cP_2(\R,2C(\alpha))$ indexed by $\epsilon$, hence also compact.
	These sets form a nested family of nonempty compact sets, so their intersection is also nonempty.
	However, their intersection is
	\beq
		S_\iota \cap \bigcap_{\epsilon > 0} \overline{\cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;\epsilon)}
		\subseteq  
		S_\iota \cap \bigcap_{\epsilon > 0} \cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;2\epsilon)
		\stackrel{\eqref{e:sM.Lip}}{=} 
		S_\iota \cap \cM^{\Lip}(\alpha)
		\stackrel{\textup{Thm.~\ref{thm:control.problems.main}}}{=} S_\iota \cap \ocM^{\Ising}(\alpha)
		= \emptyset\,,
	\eeq
which yields a contradiction.
This proves that there exists $\epsilon$ such that $\bbW_\fq(\mu,\ocM^{\Ising}(\alpha)) \le \iota$ for all $\mu \in \cM^{\Lip}(\alpha;\epsilon)$.
	The analogous claim for $\cM^{\Lip,\sym}(\alpha;\epsilon)$ and $\ocM^{\Ising,\sym}(\alpha)$ is proved similarly, using Theorem~\ref{thm:control.problems.sym} in place of Theorem~\ref{thm:control.problems.main} in \eqref{e:confinement.cM.lip.to.nbd.of.ideal}.
\end{proof}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["H is a complex Hilbert space","T is closed and symmetric (densely defined)","for (4): a conjugation C commuting with T and preserving D(T)","for (5): T is bounded below"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:53:42.770296+00:00","domain":"functional analysis, spectral theory, quantum mechanics","id":"claim_fef73e82220c1605ab1687b464def45e92df0b81dcaad18abcd8ead67320c0b8","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let T be a closed symmetric operator on a complex Hilbert space H, with deficiency subspaces K_+ = ker(T* − i), K_- = ker(T* + i) and deficiency indices n_± = dim K_±. Then: (1) D(T*) = D(T) ⊕ K_+ ⊕ K_-, a direct sum which is orthogonal for the graph inner product ⟨x, y⟩ + ⟨T*x, T*y⟩. (2) The closed symmetric extensions of T correspond bijectively to partial isometries from a closed subspace of K_+ into K_-; the self-adjoint extensions correspond bijectively to unitary operators U: K_+ → K_- (onto), via D(T_U) = {x + φ + Uφ : x ∈ D(T), φ ∈ K_+} and T_U(x + φ + Uφ) = Tx + iφ − iUφ. (3) Hence T has a self-adjoint extension iff n_+ = n_-; T is self-adjoint iff n_+ = n_- = 0; if n_+ = n_- = n with 1 ≤ n < ∞, the self-adjoint extensions form a family parametrized by the unitary group U(n); if exactly one of n_± is 0 and the other is not, T is maximal symmetric and has no self-adjoint extension. (4) If there is a conjugation C (antiunitary, C² = I) with C D(T) ⊂ D(T) and TC = CT, then n_+ = n_- (von Neumann's conjugation criterion; e.g. real differential operators with real coefficients). (5) If T is bounded below, n_+ = n_- (and a self-adjoint extension with the same lower bound exists, the Friedrichs extension).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-09-03T17:05:27.627086+00:00","domain":"measure theory","id":"claim_ff59d2398b1d8908abce8ec01c01a24a737fa38a46423f1defdc0f7bb6f05a02","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let X be a topological space. The Borel sigma-algebra B(X) is the smallest sigma-algebra of subsets of X containing every open set (equivalently, every closed set); its members are the Borel sets. It is the intersection of all sigma-algebras containing the topology, so it exists and is unique. On the real line, B(R) is generated equally by the open intervals, by the closed intervals, by the half-lines (-infinity, a] with a rational, or by any base of the topology; every open, closed, F_sigma (countable union of closed sets) and G_delta (countable intersection of open sets) set is Borel, and the Borel sets are stratified by the Borel hierarchy of countable length omega_1. B(R^n) equals the product sigma-algebra of n copies of B(R). Every continuous map between topological spaces is Borel measurable (preimages of Borel sets are Borel), as is every pointwise limit of a sequence of Borel measurable real functions; but the image of a Borel set under a continuous map need not be Borel - such images are the analytic sets (Suslin, 1917). B(R) has the cardinality of the continuum, 2^{aleph_0}, while the Lebesgue measurable sets number 2^{2^{aleph_0}} (every subset of the null Cantor set is measurable), so there exist Lebesgue measurable sets that are not Borel: Lebesgue measure on B(R) is completed by adjoining all subsets of Borel null sets. Every finite Borel measure on a Polish space is regular (inner regular by compact sets: a Radon measure), which is why Borel sets are the natural domain of measures on metric spaces.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-08-12T06:09:38.198610+00:00","domain":"general topology","id":"claim_ff61ff48cce572f4f7d51c7a320ea48eadc31611bdd1fdfe4cc31d52318be257","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"For A a subset of a topological space (X, tau), the subspace (relative) topology on A is tau_A = { A intersect U : U in tau }: its open sets are the intersections with A of open sets of X, and likewise its closed sets are the intersections with A of closed sets of X. This is a topology - it contains A and empty, and the identities (A intersect U1) intersect (A intersect U2) = A intersect (U1 intersect U2) and union of (A intersect U_i) = A intersect (union U_i) give closure under finite intersections and arbitrary unions. It is the coarsest topology making the inclusion i: A -> X continuous, since i is continuous for a topology sigma on A iff A intersect U is sigma-open for every U in tau, i.e. iff tau_A is contained in sigma. Universal property: for any space Z, a map f: Z -> A is continuous iff the composite Z -> A -> X is continuous - the property that characterizes the subspace topology.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T21:00:30.494719+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_ff77c1f088d0475912596d1b0474b612c2f8a2bac619ac99a18bb828c033a5d2","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 26 (Fixed spectrum and fixed diagonal version) of arXiv:2607.04138, 'Hives from deformed GUE minor processes'] \lab{lem:fixed-spectrum-fixed-diagonal}
Let \(w>0\) and \(u\geq 0\), and let
\[
        X=wG+uD,
\]
where \(G\) is a GUE matrix and \(D=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_n)\) is
fixed.  Let
\[
        \lambda=\spec(X),
        \qquad
        a=\diag(X).
\]
For \(1\leq k\leq n\), let \(\lambda^{(k)}\) be the ordered eigenvalue vector
of the \(k\times k\) northwest principal minor of \(X\), and write
\[
        \Gamma=(\lambda^{(1)},\ldots,\lambda^{(n)}).
\]
Then, conditional on both
\[
        \spec(X)=\lambda
        \qquad\text{and}\qquad
        \diag(X)=a,
\]
the minor process \(\Gamma\) is uniformly distributed, with respect to
Lebesgue measure, on the Gelfand-Tsetlin fiber
\[
        \GT_{\diag(\lambda)\rel a}.
\]
Equivalently, its conditional density is
\[
        \frac{1}{|\GT_{\diag(\lambda)\rel a}|}
        \mathbf 1_{\{\Gamma\in \GT_{\diag(\lambda)\rel a}\}} .
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:10:05.795845+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_ff91bb7a170547899a3b17eaa7ad9a11ddc947f90939d7baa4b872b5ddd0d1a0","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 17 of arXiv:2608.17509, '2608.17509'] Let \(\Lambda:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) be finite, \(C^1\), and strictly convex,
and define
\[
        J(x):=\sup_{\theta\in\mathbb R}\{\theta x-\Lambda(\theta)\},
        \qquad x\in\mathbb R.
\]
Set \(m_-:=\lim_{\theta\to-\infty}\Lambda'(\theta)\) and
\(m_+:=\lim_{\theta\to+\infty}\Lambda'(\theta)\), allowing infinite limits.
Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item For every \(x\in(m_-,m_+)\), the supremum defining \(J(x)\) is attained
at the unique \(\theta(x)\in\mathbb R\) satisfying
\(\Lambda'(\theta(x))=x\), and
\[
J(x)=\theta(x)x-\Lambda(\theta(x)).
\]

\item The function \(J\) is differentiable on \((m_-,m_+)\), with
\(J'(x)=\theta(x)\). In particular, \(J\) is strictly convex on
\((m_-,m_+)\).

\item For every \(\theta\in\mathbb R\),
\(J(\Lambda'(\theta))=\theta\Lambda'(\theta)-\Lambda(\theta)\).

\item If \(\Lambda(0)=0\) and \(\Lambda'(0)\in(m_-,m_+)\), then
\(J(x)\ge0\) for every \(x\in\mathbb R\), and \(J\) vanishes uniquely at
\(x=\Lambda'(0)\).
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["Lebesgue measure on R^n","M is the centered or uncentered Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:49:36.553467+00:00","domain":"harmonic analysis, maximal functions","id":"claim_ffa8aee1191447b8b8fa930b110a55716c66233d776634ca4058ba7238a266e6","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"The Hardy-Littlewood maximal inequality is WEAK type (1,1), never strong type (1,1), and Marcinkiewicz interpolation gives nothing at p = 1 (its constant contains p/(p - p_0) and blows up as p -> 1+). Precisely: if f is in L^1(R^n) and f is not a.e. 0, then Mf is NOT in L^1(R^n). Global counterexample: pick R with c = int_{B(0,R)} |f| > 0; for |x| >= R the ball B(x, 2|x|) contains B(0,R), so Mf(x) >= c / (v_n (2|x|)^n), which is not integrable at infinity. Local counterexample showing the failure is not only at infinity: f(x) = |x|^{-n} (log(1/|x|))^{-2} 1_{{|x| < 1/2}} is in L^1, but averaging over B(x, 2|x|) gives Mf(x) >= c' |x|^{-n} (log(1/|x|))^{-1} near 0, which is not locally integrable. The correct endpoint substitutes are: (i) the weak (1,1) bound |{Mf > t}| <= 3^n ||f||_1 / t; (ii) Stein's L log L theorem: for f supported in a ball B, Mf is integrable over B if and only if int_B |f| log^+ |f| < infinity. So a proof that applies 'M is bounded on L^p' at p = 1, or that interpolates strong (1,1) with strong (infinity, infinity), is wrong; the same warning applies to any operator known only to be weak (1,1), such as the Calderon-Zygmund singular integrals and the Hilbert transform.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["f is locally integrable on R^n","balls are Euclidean and |.| is Lebesgue measure"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:49:36.552000+00:00","domain":"harmonic analysis, real-variable methods","id":"claim_ffa9201fa7a9c6fdbdafe36863b70b61b6ad169b72c4ec8441e19549baf37472","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"For f in L^1_loc(R^n) (Lebesgue measure |.|), the centered Hardy-Littlewood maximal function is Mf(x) = sup_{r>0} (1/|B(x,r)|) int_{B(x,r)} |f(y)| dy, with values in [0, infinity]. The uncentered version is M'f(x) = sup over all open balls B containing x of (1/|B|) int_B |f|; one has Mf <= M'f <= 2^n Mf. The set {Mf > t} is open for every t (so Mf is lower semicontinuous, hence Borel measurable), M is sublinear, M(f) = M(|f|), and ||Mf||_infinity <= ||f||_infinity. Cubes in place of balls give a pointwise comparable operator (constants depending only on n).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T17:03:59.308541+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_ffb02b9c6b43215bb874343f746a193d36db7a3b55a74e2032c1de73fddb3049","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Satz thm:HigherOrderPI of arXiv:2507.08692, 'Some notes on higher order concentration of measure'] Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on ${\mathbb R}^n$ which satisfies a Poincar\'{e}-type inequality with constant $\sigma^2 > 0$, and let $f\colon {\mathbb R}^n \to {\mathbb R}$ be a $\mathcal{C}^d$-smooth function with ${\mathbb E} f = 0$.
